---
name: fnstools
description: "Drive an installed FNSTools toolkit from a coding agent. Use when a TouchDesigner project holds FNS_ COMPs or op.FNS_ shortcuts, when the user mentions FNSTools, the Hub, the FNS toolbar or quick-launch commands, or asks what an FNS tool does and how to call it from code."
---

# FNSTools

FNSTools is a toolkit of TouchDesigner components by Function Store
(https://functionstore.tools): workflow tools, additions to TouchDesigner's own
UI, and operators. It is installed once per machine into the user palette
folder, `<user palette>/FNSTools` (TouchDesigner's `app.userPaletteFolder`),
and placed into a project as one root COMP whose children are the installed
packages. This bundle was generated from the release named in `VERSION`;
`references/index.md` lists every package it covers.

The skill does not depend on a bridge. With an MCP bridge into TouchDesigner
(Envoy or any other) the agent calls the methods below directly; without one
it writes the same calls into scripts or DATs the user runs.

## Where things are

- `op.FNS` is the toolkit root COMP in the project. `op.FNS.op('FNS_BeatMod')`
  reaches an installed package by its COMP name. The root carries two pulses,
  `Picktools` (install and remove tools) and `Opensettings` (every tool's
  settings on one page), and a table DAT named `installed` that records each
  installed package with the artifact hash, release and time it came from.
- Package COMP names keep the `FNS_` prefix (`FNS_BeatMod`); every listing a
  user reads shows the public name (BeatMod). Shortcuts, file names and
  command keys keep the prefix too.
- Not every package is a child of the root: a member of the FNS operator
  family is placed from the FNS tab of the OP Create dialog, like a stock
  operator, and a few tools are installed beside the toolkit at the project
  root. The package page's "Reach it" section says where each one is.
- The machine folder `<user palette>/FNSTools/` holds `store/` (one tox per
  package plus `manifest.json`, the mirror the installer and updater read),
  `config/FNStools_config.json` (roaming settings), `tables/` (externalised
  tables such as the hotkey table), `OpTemplates/` (the global template
  library), `FNS/` (the operator family, one tox and one json sidecar per
  member) and `agent-skill/` (this bundle).
- `op.FNS_UPDATER` is the updater: `Installed()` is the project's install
  record, `Compare()` reports what the store has newer bytes for without
  touching the network, `CheckUpdates()` fetches the manifest and compares,
  `UpdateProject()` replaces only the packages that differ, keeping settings.

## How a package is reached

- A package with a global shortcut is reached by it from anywhere in the
  project: `op.FNS_UPDATER`, `op.FNS_HOTKEY_MANAGER`, `op.FNS_BEATMOD`. The
  package page and `references/index.md` name it. A package without one is
  reached by its COMP (`op.FNS.op('CookBar')`) or by the placed copy.
- The promoted API of a package is the set of `UpperCamelCase` members of its
  extension, called on the COMP itself: `op.FNS_UPDATER.Compare()`. A
  `lowerCamelCase` member is the package's own wiring (reached only as
  `comp.ext.<ExtensionName>.method()`, where the name is the extension's
  Extension Name parameter, not its class name); a `_leading` member is
  private. Each package page lists the promoted API with signatures and the
  first line of each docstring, reflected from the shipped build.
- Promoted members are resolved by the COMP's attribute lookup, so they do
  not appear in `dir(comp)`; the package page is the listing.
- A package's own settings are its custom parameters: `op.FNS_BEATMOD.par.Bpm`.
  Each page ends with the parameter list (name, label, style, default, help).
- `Access` on a page names the tier the package needs: Free, or a Patreon
  tier. A tier package installs only for an account that holds it; the page's
  Docs link is the same page the user sees on the website.

## The registries

Thirteen registries own the toolkit's shared surfaces: the toolbar, the pane
bars, the main menu, the OP Create dialog, the pane-type menu, the console,
the Hub's tabs, the Palette Browser, the timeline, the find bar, the network
overlay, the quick-launch commands and the settings file. Each runs as one
global promoted into `/sys/FNS_Registries` and is reached by its shortcut
(`op.FNS_CONFIGREGISTRY`, `op.FNS_TOOLBARREGISTRY`, ...). A tool joins a
surface by registering with the registry (`RegisterWidget`, `RegisterTab`,
`RegisterTool`, ...) and the registry owns the surface, its tables and its
files from then on. `references/registries.md` has every registry, what it
owns, how a tool joins it and what a consumer reads from it.

## Quick-launch commands

Tools declare commands, and `op.FNS_COMMANDREGISTRY` collects them for the
in-TouchDesigner command palette (FNS_CommandPalette) and the TDX launcher.

- `op.FNS_COMMANDREGISTRY.Commands()` is the live list: one dict per command
  with `key`, `tool`, `id`, `label`, `help`, `path` and, where the command
  declares it, `state`.
- `op.FNS_COMMANDREGISTRY.Run(key, args=None, kwargs=None)` runs one. The
  key is the declaring COMP's path, `#`, and the command's id:
  `op.FNS.op('FNS_Updater').path + '#checkforupdates'` for a package's own
  command, and for one a COMP inside the package declares (the built-in
  TouchDesigner commands under FNS_CommandRegistry, for example)
  `op.FNS.op('FNS_CommandRegistry/FNS_BuiltinCommands/TD_Session').path + '#togglerealtime'`.
  `Commands()` rows carry the live key.
- A command is a promoted method of the COMP that declares it, so the
  method can also be called on that COMP directly.
- `references/commands.md` lists every command of every public package with
  its label, id, help, method, declaring COMP and parameters; the package
  page repeats its own.

## Op alternatives

A stock operator type may have FNS alternatives: a package page's
"Alternative for" section and the index line name the types. When the user
creates such an operator from the OP Create dialog with the gate held (the
`Shortcutalternatives` parameter on the op-menu registry's Alternatives page,
default `alt ctrl`), a popup offers the alternatives, and the chosen one is
placed in the operator's place with every input and output reconnected. A
package that is only in the store is offered too and fetched before it is
placed; placing is a place, not an install. From code,
`op.FNS_OPMENUREGISTRY.Alternatives` is the merged `{opType: [alternative,
...]}` and `op.FNS_OPMENUREGISTRY.PlaceAlternative(orig_op, alternative)`
does the placement.

## Settings and hotkeys

- Settings persist through `op.FNS_CONFIGREGISTRY`: every registered tool's
  custom parameters are written as one section of the aggregated file
  (`ConfigPath` is its absolute path), globally in
  `<user palette>/FNSTools/config/FNStools_config.json` or inside the `.toe`
  when the root's `Configscope` parameter is `project`
  (`SetConfigScope('global' | 'project', prompt=False)` flips it).
  `SaveAll()` and `LoadAll()` snapshot and re-apply every tool; `SaveTool(name)`
  and `LoadTool(name)` do one. A setting is changed by setting the tool's
  parameter; the registry writes the file.
- Hotkeys are custom parameters on the tools, holding a combo such as `alt.g`
  or `ctrl.shift.g`. `op.FNS_HOTKEY_MANAGER.Discover()` lists every binding in
  the project with its owner, parameter and current value, `ComputeConflicts()`
  the combos bound more than once, `ApplyBinding(display_path, par_name, combo)`
  rebinds one, `ResetToDefault(display_path, par_name)` restores the
  parameter's default, and `SaveHotkeys()` writes the gathered table under
  `<user palette>/FNSTools/tables/`. Each package page's Hotkeys section is
  that discovery, taken at build time.
- The Hub is the manager window: the FNS button in the main-menu bar opens
  it, as does `op.FNS.op('FNS_Hub').Open(tab=None)`. The console is the
  toolkit's web front, served from inside the project:
  `op.FNS_CONSOLE.Open(tab=None)` shows it and `Url()` is its address while
  it serves.

## One fact the network does not show

`op.FNS` exists only while the toolkit root is in the project. A package can
also run on its own, as a single tox dropped into a project with no toolkit
root, and then there is no `op.FNS` and no registry globals. Code that may run
in both places tests `hasattr(op, 'FNS')` before using either.

## Finding out more

`references/index.md` (one line per package: category, summary, docs link,
shortcut, what it is an alternative for), then `references/<Package>.md`
(what it does, how it is reached, the promoted API, commands, hotkeys,
requirements, parameters), then the page's Docs link for the full
user-facing documentation.

# ChopBank

A bank of channel processors: one block per channel, each with its own range, exponent curve, zero-below, lag and speed mode, built from the input with one Snap Input, with gain before and after and every block promoted as a property. An alternative for the Math CHOP and the Constant CHOP.

- Category: CHOPs & sensing
- Version: 1.0.5
- Access: Base
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/chopbank/

## What it does

- **Shape each channel with its own block**: Each block shapes one channel with its own range remap, exponent curve, Zero Below, lag, and a speed mode that turns it into a running total.
- **Build the bank with Snap Input**: One press makes a block for every incoming channel, named after it and holding its value; a new block copies the previous block's settings.
- **Add channels the input lacks**: A block with no matching input channel outputs its own Value, so the bank can add channels.
- **Gain before and after**: Master gain on every channel before the blocks and after them.
- **Replace a Math or Constant CHOP**: Create a Math CHOP or Constant CHOP with the alternatives shortcut held and ChopBank is offered in its place, wired into the same spot.
- **Blocks as properties**: Each block is a property on the node, so Python reads and sets its Value by name.

## Reach it

No global shortcut. Place a copy: it is the FNS operator family member `chopBank` (Chop Bank) on the FNS tab of the OP Create dialog, also at `<user palette>/FNSTools/FNS/ChopBank.tox`. Its promoted methods are called on the placed copy.

## Promoted API

- `Chan1` (property): The Value parameter of the block named 'chan1'; assign to set it.
- `Chan1_out` (property): The output of the block named 'chan1': the channel value for a number, else the table cell.
- `CompEditorExt` (attribute)
- `ConsumeParGroup(size: int, previous_size: int)`: Grow the sequence's block size to hold a multi-value Value parameter group of `size` components.
- `IsParGroup` (property): Returns whether the current parameter is a parameter group
- `OnAdd(block_idx: int, prev_name: str = None)`: Create, or rename, the promoted attribute pair of one block; called when a block is added or its Name changes.
- `OnPrefixChanged(old_prefix: str)`: Rebuild the promoted per-block attributes after the Prefix parameter changed from old_prefix.
- `OnTypeChanged(new_type: str)`: Rebuild every block's Value parameter in the new style (Float, Int, RGB, ...); called when the Type parameter changes.
- `OnValChanged(block_idx, _val)`: Called when a block's Value parameter changes; currently a no-op, the dependency update is disabled.
- `ParGroupChannels` (property): Returns a list of channel names for the parameter group, or an empty list if not a parameter group
- `ParGroupSize` (property): Returns the size of the parameter group, or 1 if not a parameter group
- `RefreshAllAttributes(old_prefix: str = None)`: Remove every promoted per-block attribute and create them again from the current blocks (when Promote is on).
- `SeqConst` (property): The sequence of constant blocks this tool manages (the Seqname sequence on the owner).

## Commands

No commands recorded for this package.

## Hotkeys

None.

## Alternative for

- `constantCHOP`
- `mathCHOP`

## Requires

- `FNS_OpMenuRegistry`

## Parameters

### Bank

- **In Scope** (`par.Scope`, Str), default `*`: Which input channels the bank takes, as a pattern like fader* . Only asked when the input has more than one channel.
- **Gain Pre** (`par.Mastergainpre`, Float), default `1.0`: Gain on every input channel before the bank processes it.
- **Gain Post** (`par.Mastergainpost`, Float), default `1.0`: Gain on every output channel after the bank.
- **Snap Input** (`par.Snapinput`, Pulse): Rebuild the bank from the input: one block per channel, named after it and holding its current value.
- **Bank** (`par.Bank`, Sequence), default `0`: One block per channel. Add a block to process one more channel.
- **Name** (`par.Bank0name`, Str): The input channel this block processes, and its output name. Empty takes the channel at this block's position. A name the input does not have makes a new channel from Value.
- **Value** (`par.Bank0value`, Float), default `0.0`: The value this block outputs while no input channel matches it.
- **Math** (`par.Bank0math`, Header)
- **Type** (`par.Bank0type`, Menu), default `off`, menu `off`, `clamp`, `loop`, `zigzag`: What happens outside the From Range: off lets values through, clamp holds them at the ends, loop wraps them round, zigzag bounces them back.
- **From Range** (`par.Bank0fromrange`, Float x2), default `0.0`: The input range. With Type set to clamp, loop or zigzag this is also the limit.
- **To Range** (`par.Bank0torange`, Float x2), default `0.0`: The output range the From Range maps onto.
- **Zero Below** (`par.Bank0zerobelow`, Toggle), default `off`: Output 0 while the input sits at the bottom of the From Range, instead of the bottom of the To Range. Only with Type set to clamp.
- **Exponent Value** (`par.Bank0expval`, Float), default `1.0`: Exponent for the curve between the ranges: 1 is linear, above 1 eases in, below 1 eases out.
- **Lag** (`par.Bank0lag`, Float x2), default `0.0`: Seconds to glide up and down toward a new value.
- **Speed** (`par.Bank0speed1`, Header)
- **Is Speed** (`par.Bank0isspeed`, Toggle), default `off`: Treat the processed value as a speed and output its running total instead, so a held input keeps moving.
- **Limit Type** (`par.Bank0limittype`, Menu), default `off`, menu `off`, `clamp`, `loop`, `zigzag`: What happens when the running total leaves Minimum and Maximum.
- **Minimum** (`par.Bank0min`, Float), default `0.0`: Lower limit for the running total.
- **Maximum** (`par.Bank0max`, Float), default `1.0`: Upper limit for the running total.
- **Reset Value** (`par.Bank0resetvalue`, Float), default `0.0`: The value the running total returns to on reset.
- **Reset** (`par.Bank0reset`, Toggle), default `off`: Hold the running total at the Reset Value while on.
- **Reset Pulse** (`par.Bank0resetpulse`, Pulse): Return the running total to the Reset Value once.

### Common

- **Promote to Property** (`par.Promote`, Toggle), default `on`: Expose each block as a property on this COMP, named after the block, that reads and sets its Value.
- **To get/set values as .{prefix}{name}** (`par.Header`, Header)
- **Property Prefix** (`par.Prefix`, Str), default `C_`: Put in front of every property name, to keep them clear of other names on the COMP.
- **Author: Function Store (@function.str)** (`par.Author`, Header)

# ChopProcess

Shapes channels in one node: limit, remap between ranges with an exponent curve, zero at the bottom, lag, and an optional speed mode that turns the result into a running total. An alternative for the Math CHOP.

- Category: CHOPs & sensing
- Version: 1.0.5
- Access: Base
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/chopprocess/

## What it does

- **Limit and remap with a curve**: Limits incoming values to a range and remaps that range onto another through an exponent curve.
- **Zero Below**: Makes the bottom of the input range output 0, so a fader switches fully off at its lowest point yet starts usefully once moved.
- **Lag smoothing**: Glides toward new values with a lag.
- **Speed mode**: Treats the result as a speed and outputs its running total, which can be clamped, looped or bounced between limits.
- **Shape a whole fader bank in one node**: Every input channel goes through the same chain, so one node shapes a whole fader bank; with nothing connected, the Value parameter is processed.
- **Replace a Math CHOP**: Create a Math CHOP with the alternatives shortcut held and ChopProcess is offered in its place, wired into the same spot.

## Reach it

No global shortcut. Place a copy: it is the FNS operator family member `chopProcess` (Chop Process) on the FNS tab of the OP Create dialog, also at `<user palette>/FNSTools/FNS/ChopProcess.tox`. Its promoted methods are called on the placed copy.

## Promoted API

No promoted API: the package has no extension. Its parameters, listed below, are its surface.

## Commands

No commands recorded for this package.

## Hotkeys

None.

## Alternative for

- `mathCHOP`

## Requires

- `FNS_OpMenuRegistry`

## Parameters

### Custom

- **Value** (`par.Value`, Float), default `0.0`: The value to process when nothing is wired into the input.
- **Name** (`par.Name`, Str): Rename the output channels: names separated by spaces, one per channel, or a pattern like chan[1-4]. Empty keeps the input's names.
- **Type** (`par.Type`, Menu), default `off`, menu `off`, `clamp`, `loop`, `zigzag`: What happens outside the From Range: off lets values through, clamp holds them at the ends, loop wraps them round, zigzag bounces them back.
- **From Range** (`par.Fromrange`, Float x2), default `-1.0`: The input range. With Type set to clamp, loop or zigzag this is also the limit.
- **To Range** (`par.Torange`, Float x2), default `0.0`: The output range the From Range maps onto.
- **Zero Below** (`par.Zerobelow`, Toggle), default `off`: Output 0 while the input sits at the bottom of the From Range, instead of the bottom of the To Range. Only with Type set to clamp.
- **Exponent Value** (`par.Expval`, Float), default `2.0`: Exponent for the curve between the ranges: 1 is linear, above 1 eases in, below 1 eases out.
- **Lag** (`par.Lag`, Float x2), default `0.2`: Seconds to glide up and down toward a new value.
- **Speed** (`par.Speed`, Header)
- **Is Speed** (`par.Isspeed`, Toggle), default `off`: Treat the processed value as a speed and output its running total instead, so a held input keeps moving.
- **Limit Type** (`par.Limittype`, Menu), default `off`, menu `off`, `clamp`, `loop`, `zigzag`: What happens when the running total leaves Minimum and Maximum.
- **Minimum** (`par.Min`, Float), default `0.0`: Lower limit for the running total.
- **Maximum** (`par.Max`, Float), default `1.0`: Upper limit for the running total.
- **Reset Value** (`par.Resetvalue`, Float), default `0.0`: The value the running total returns to on reset.
- **Reset** (`par.Reset`, Toggle), default `off`: Hold the running total at the Reset Value while on.
- **Reset Pulse** (`par.Resetpulse`, Pulse): Return the running total to the Reset Value once.

# CircularDistortionTOP

A circular distortion for images: rings of displacement around a centre you place, with phase, frequency, amplitude and a mode blend, and a choice of how the input extends past its edge.

- Category: Visual
- Version: 1.0.5
- Access: Base
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/circulardistortiontop/

## What it does

- **Ring distortion around a centre you place**: Pushes the image in rings around any point: the middle of the frame, a face, a logo.
- **Animate the rings with Phase**: Animating Phase sends the rings outward or inward; a step of 1 moves them by one ring.
- **Round on any aspect**: The rings stay circular on a 16:9 frame or any other non-square image.
- **Blend between two distortion modes**: Mode blends between a push that grows with the distance from the centre and one that is the same strength everywhere.
- **Edge handling**: Choose what shows where the rings pull in pixels from past the image edge: hold, zero, repeat or mirror.

## Reach it

No global shortcut. Place a copy: it is the FNS operator family member `circularDistortion` (Circular Distortion) on the FNS tab of the OP Create dialog, also at `<user palette>/FNSTools/FNS/CircularDistortionTOP.tox`. Its promoted methods are called on the placed copy.

## Promoted API

No promoted API: the package has no extension. Its parameters, listed below, are its surface.

## Commands

No commands recorded for this package.

## Hotkeys

None.

## Alternative for

None.

## Requires

Nothing.

## Parameters

### Custom

- **Center** (`par.Center`, XYZW x2), default `0.5`: The point the rings are centred on, in UV: 0.5, 0.5 is the middle of the image.
- **Phase** (`par.Phase`, Float), default `0.5`: Shifts the rings outward or inward; one full step (0 to 1) moves them one ring. Animate it to make them travel.
- **Frequency** (`par.Frequency`, Float), default `0.5`: How tightly the rings are packed: higher values put more rings across the image.
- **Amplitude** (`par.Amplitude`, Float), default `0.5`: How far the rings displace the image. 0 leaves it untouched.
- **Mode** (`par.Mode`, Float), default `1.0`: Blends two ways of distorting: 0 scales the image radially around the centre, 1 pushes each pixel along its direction from the centre.
- **Input Extend Mode Uv** (`par.Inputextenduv`, Menu), default `mirror`, menu `hold`, `zero`, `repeat`, `mirror`: What a displaced sample returns outside the image: hold the edge, zero, repeat or mirror.

# ColorGen

A colour palette generator: a lookup of any length shaped by a phase step per channel and per channel exponents, with a lookup ramp as a second output.

- Category: Visual
- Version: 1.0.4
- Access: Base
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/colorgen/

## What it does

- **Palette from a formula**: Red, green and blue follow one curve, offset from each other by a phase step and bent by an exponent each, so a few values give a whole family of gradients.
- **Animate with one Phase**: One Phase value scrolls the palette and lands back where it started at 1, so it loops cleanly when you animate it.
- **Palette strip**: out_col is the palette as a colour strip, as many pixels wide as the palette has colours, ready for a Lookup TOP.
- **Colour an image through the palette**: out_lookup colours the input image through the palette; with nothing wired, a built-in 0 to 1 ramp shows the palette.

## Reach it

No global shortcut. Place a copy: it is the FNS operator family member `colorGen` (Color Gen) on the FNS tab of the OP Create dialog, also at `<user palette>/FNSTools/FNS/ColorGen.tox`. Its promoted methods are called on the placed copy.

## Promoted API

No promoted API: the package has no extension. Its parameters, listed below, are its surface.

## Commands

No commands recorded for this package.

## Hotkeys

None.

## Alternative for

None.

## Requires

Nothing.

## Parameters

### Custom

- **Length** (`par.Length`, Int), default `255`: Number of colours in the palette: the width in pixels of out_col, and of the fallback ramp that feeds the lookup when nothing is connected to the input.
- **Phase Step per Channel** (`par.Phasestep`, Float), default `0.101`: Phase offset between the R, G and B curves: R stays put, B is shifted by twice this many palette cycles, G by a share of that set by Exponent Shift. 0 keeps the channels in step (greys).
- **Phase** (`par.Phase`, Float), default `0.0`: Scrolls all three curves along the palette. 1 is one full cycle and lands back where it started; 0.5 mirrors the palette. Animate it to cycle the colours.
- **Exponent Shift** (`par.Expval`, Float), default `1.0`: Exponent that places G's phase between R and B: 1 puts it halfway, higher values move it toward R, values below 1 toward B.
- **Exponent R** (`par.Expval1`, Float), default `1.0`: Exponent shaping the red curve along the palette: 1 is linear, higher values keep the channel dark for longer, below 1 brightens it early.
- **Exponent G** (`par.Expval2`, Float), default `1.0`: Exponent shaping the green curve along the palette: 1 is linear, higher values keep the channel dark for longer, below 1 brightens it early.
- **Exponent B** (`par.Expval3`, Float), default `1.0`: Exponent shaping the blue curve along the palette: 1 is linear, higher values keep the channel dark for longer, below 1 brightens it early.

# ColorGenPro

A cosine palette generator in GLSL: the full coefficient set per channel, an RGB and D mode, blackout and soft regions, and a lookup ramp as a second output.

- Category: Visual
- Version: 1.0.4
- Access: Pro
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/colorgenpro/

## What it does

- **Cosine palette with every coefficient**: Offset, amplitude, period, phase and exponent for red, green and blue, for smooth gradients that loop cleanly.
- **RGB and D mode**: Drives the three phases from one Offset, Amplitude and Exponent, so a single value scrolls the whole palette.
- **Blackout region**: Keeps the start of the palette black, added to the length or taken from the colours, with a soft edge you shape.
- **Palette strip output**: out_col is the palette as a colour strip, and Length sets how many colours it holds.
- **Colour an image through the palette**: out_lookup colours the input image through the palette; with nothing wired a built-in 0 to 1 ramp shows the palette.
- **Reset to the shipped coefficients**: Default restores the shipped coefficients and leaves any parameter driven by an expression alone.

## Reach it

No global shortcut. Place a copy: it is the FNS operator family member `colorGenPro` (Color Gen Pro) on the FNS tab of the OP Create dialog, also at `<user palette>/FNSTools/FNS/ColorGenPro.tox`. Its promoted methods are called on the placed copy.

## Promoted API

No promoted API: the package has no extension. Its parameters, listed below, are its surface.

## Commands

No commands recorded for this package.

## Hotkeys

None.

## Alternative for

None.

## Requires

Nothing.

## Parameters

### Custom

- **Length** (`par.Length`, Int), default `256`: Number of colours in the palette (the width of out_col). Blackout with Reductive at 0 adds its share on top of this.
- **Input Smoothness** (`par.Inputfiltertype`, Menu), default `linear`, menu `nearest`, `linear`, `mipmap`: Sampling filter the lookup uses on the input image: Nearest picks exact palette entries, Linear blends between neighbours.
- **Blackout** (`par.Blackout`, Float), default `0.0`: Share of the palette (0 to 1) that fades to black at its start. Reductive decides whether that share is added to the length or taken from the colours; above 0 it enables the Soften parameters.
- **Reductive** (`par.Lensubtract`, Float), default `0.0`: How Blackout makes room: 0 extends the palette by the blackout share, 1 keeps Length and takes the blackout from the colours.
- **Soften Black** (`par.Blacksoften`, Float), default `0.5`: Width of the fade from black into the palette, as a share of the blackout region. 0 is a hard edge, 1 fades across the whole region.
- **Soften Exponent** (`par.Softenexponent`, Float), default `1.0`: Curve of the black fade: 1 is linear, higher values stay dark longer, below 1 brighten early.
- **Soften Extend** (`par.Softenextend`, Menu), default `Zero`, menu `Mirror`, `Zero`, `Repeat`: What the palette does inside the blackout region under the fade: Mirror reflects it, Zero/Hold holds the first colour, Repeat continues the cycle backwards.
- **pow(a + b*cos( 2PI * (c*t+d) ), e)** (`par.Header`, Header): The cosine palette formula each channel follows; t runs 0 to 1 along the palette.
- **a (Offset)** (`par.A`, Float x3), default `0.5`: a (Offset) for red, green, blue: the base brightness the cosine swings around.
- **b (Amplitude)** (`par.B`, Float x3), default `0.5`: b (Amplitude) for red, green, blue: how far the cosine swings above and below a. Values above a clip to black at the troughs.
- **c (Period)** (`par.C`, Float x3), default `1.0`: c (Period) for red, green, blue: how many colour cycles fit along the palette.
- **d (Phase)** (`par.D`, Float x3), default `0.0`: d (Phase) for red, green, blue: shifts each channel's cycle; offsetting the three is what makes hues. Driven by Offset, Amplitude and Exponent while RGBD Mode is on.
- **e (Exponent)** (`par.E`, Float x3), default `1.0`: e (Exponent) for red, green, blue: gamma on each channel; above 1 deepens, below 1 lifts.
- **RGBD Mode** (`par.Rgbdmode`, Toggle), default `off`: Drive the three d (Phase) values from Offset, Amplitude and Exponent instead of setting them by hand. Switching it on restores the shipped coefficients first.
- **Offset** (`par.Offset`, Float), default `0.0`: RGBD Mode: phase of the red channel; green and blue follow from it.
- **Amplitude** (`par.Amplitude`, Float), default `0.2`: RGBD Mode: phase spread from red to blue. 0 puts all three channels in phase (greys).
- **Exponent** (`par.Exponent`, Float), default `1.0`: RGBD Mode: where green sits between red and blue in the spread: 1 halfway, higher values toward red.
- **Default** (`par.Default`, Pulse): Restore the shipped coefficients (a, b, c, d, e) and the RGBD Offset, Amplitude and Exponent. Parameters driven by an expression are left alone.

# ComplexMix

Combines two UV fields as complex numbers: add, subtract, multiply, divide or raise one to the other, optionally weighted by a third input, then samples an image through the result.

- Category: Visual
- Version: 1.0.4
- Access: Free
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/complexmix/

## What it does

- **Combine two UV fields as complex numbers**: Treats each pixel pair of two UV fields as complex numbers and adds, subtracts, multiplies, divides or raises one to the other.
- **Weighting between the operands**: Fn Weight balances the two operands before they combine, so with Add one warp can morph into the other.
- **Sample an image through the result**: Samples the in1 image through the combined coordinates, so two ComplexOp warps become their sum, product or quotient.
- **Transform the combined coordinates**: Moves, rotates and scales the combined coordinates, with Aspect keeping rotation and scale round on a non-square output.
- **Blend the effect in**: Blend fades from the plain image to the full combination; animate it to bring the warp in on a cue.
- **Chain the combined UV field**: out2 outputs the combined UV field for chaining into another sampler.

## Reach it

No global shortcut. Place a copy: it is the FNS operator family member `complexMix` (Complex Mix) on the FNS tab of the OP Create dialog, also at `<user palette>/FNSTools/FNS/ComplexMix.tox`. Its promoted methods are called on the placed copy.

## Promoted API

No promoted API: the package has no extension. Its parameters, listed below, are its surface.

## Commands

No commands recorded for this package.

## Hotkeys

None.

Nothing.

## Parameters

### Custom

- **Operation** (`par.Operation`, Menu), default `Add`, menu `Op1`, `Op2`, `Add`, `Subtract`, `Multiply`, `Divide`, `Power1**2`, `Power2**1`: How the two complex operands (input 2 = Op1, input 3 = Op2, read from their red/green channels) combine: either one alone, or complex add, subtract, multiply, divide or power.
- **Weighting** (`par.Weighting`, Toggle), default `off`: Scales Op1 by (1 - Fn Weight) and Op2 by Fn Weight before they combine. Not used by Op1 only / Op2 only.
- **Fn Weight** (`par.Fnweight`, Float), default `0.5`: Balance between the operands when Weighting is on: 0 is all Op1, 1 is all Op2.
- **Aspect** (`par.Aspect`, Toggle), default `off`: Applies the transform in aspect-corrected space so rotation and scale stay round on non-square outputs.
- **Transform Order** (`par.Xord`, Menu), default `srt`, menu `srt`, `str`, `rst`, `rts`, `tsr`, `trs`: Order in which the transform applies scale, rotate and translate to the combined coordinates.
- **Trans** (`par.Mixtrans`, Float x2), default `0.0`: Moves the combined coordinates along x and y.
- **Rot** (`par.Rot`, Float), default `0.0`: Rotates the combined coordinates by this many degrees around the pivot.
- **Scale** (`par.Mixscale`, Float x2), default `1.0`: Scales the combined coordinates along x and y; larger values zoom in.
- **Pivot** (`par.Pivot`, Float x2), default `0.0`: Pivot (x, y): the point that rotation and scale happen around.
- **Extend** (`par.Mode`, Menu), default `Mirror`, menu `Hold`, `Zero`, `Repeat`, `Mirror`: How input 1 is sampled where the coordinates leave 0..1: Hold the edge pixels, Zero (transparent black), Repeat the image, or Mirror it.

# ComplexOp

Treats the image plane as the complex plane and applies a complex function to it: square, root, exp, log, the trigonometric and hyperbolic families, with iteration, a pre and post transform and a choice of edge handling.

- Category: Visual
- Version: 1.0.4
- Access: Free
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/complexop/

## What it does

- **Warp an image through a complex function**: Reads each pixel's UV as a complex number, runs it through the chosen function and samples the input image at the result.
- **Function menu: square, root, exp, log, sin and more**: Offers square, root, exp, log, inverse, power, and the trigonometric and hyperbolic families with their inverses.
- **Iteration**: Applies the function up to 64 times in a row, with an escape radius that can stop it early.
- **Transform before and after the function**: A transform before and after the function moves the point of interest to where the function does something worth seeing.
- **Edge handling**: Extend picks what fills the frame where the warped coordinates leave the image: hold the edge, zero, repeat or mirror.
- **Border mask output**: The borders output keeps the mapped image only near the edges of each repeated tile, with Borders setting where that soft edge starts.
- **Chain functions through the UV output**: A second output carries the mapped UV field, for a second ComplexOp, ComplexMix or a Remap TOP.

## Reach it

No global shortcut. Place a copy: it is the FNS operator family member `complexOp` (Complex Op) on the FNS tab of the OP Create dialog, also at `<user palette>/FNSTools/FNS/ComplexOp.tox`. Its promoted methods are called on the placed copy.

## Promoted API

No promoted API: the package has no extension. Its parameters, listed below, are its surface.

## Commands

No commands recorded for this package.

## Hotkeys

None.

## Alternative for

None.

## Requires

Nothing.

## Parameters

### Custom

- **Operand/Map** (`par.Uv`, Toggle), default `off`: On: the input is an image, warped through the function over a screen-space complex plane (Center/Aspect apply). Off: the input red/green channels ARE the complex operand, for chaining the UV output of another Complex Op.
- **Op** (`par.Op`, Menu), default `none`, menu `none`, `csqr`, `csqrt`, `cexp`, `clog`, `cinv`, `cabs2`, `cconj`, `csin`, `ccos`, `ctan`, `ccot`, `csinh`, `ccosh`, `ctanh`, `ccoth`, `casin`, `cacos`, `catan`, `cacot`, `casinh`, `cacosh`, `catanh`, `cacoth`, `cpolar`, `cpow`, `cconst`: The complex function applied to z. None passes z through, so only the transforms and Extend act.
- **Power** (`par.Power`, Float), default `2.0`: Base of the logarithm for Logarithm, or the exponent n for Power (z^n). Enabled only for those two functions.
- **Const** (`par.Const`, Float x2), default `0.0`: Real and imaginary part of the constant returned by the Constant function (enabled only for Constant).
- **Op Iter** (`par.Opiter`, Int), default `1`: How many times the function is applied in a row (1-64). Higher values fold the image further; Boundary can stop the iteration early.
- **Center UV** (`par.Center`, Toggle), default `off`: Map mode only. Puts the complex origin at the image centre (z runs -1..1) instead of the bottom-left corner (0..1). With Op None the result is the image tiled by the Extend mode.
- **Aspect** (`par.Aspect`, Toggle), default `off`: Map mode only. Scales the complex plane by the image aspect so circles stay round on non-square images.
- **Transform Order** (`par.Xord`, Menu), default `srt`, menu `srt`, `str`, `rst`, `rts`, `tsr`, `trs`: Order in which the pre transform applies scale, rotate and translate to z before the function.
- **Trans** (`par.Optrans`, Float x2), default `0.0`: Pre transform: moves z along x and y before the function.
- **Rot** (`par.Rot`, Float), default `0.0`: Pre transform: rotates z by this many degrees before the function.
- **Scale** (`par.Opscale`, Float x2), default `1.0`: Pre transform: scales z along x and y before the function.
- **Pivot** (`par.Pivot`, Float x2), default `0.0`: Pre transform pivot (x, y): the point that rotation and scale happen around.
- **Post Transform Order** (`par.Xord2`, Menu), default `srt`, menu `srt`, `str`, `rst`, `rts`, `tsr`, `trs`: Order in which the post transform applies scale, rotate and translate to the result of the function.
- **Post Trans** (`par.Posttrans`, Float x2), default `0.0`: Post transform: moves the result along x and y after the function.
- **Post Rot** (`par.Postrot`, Float), default `0.0`: Post transform: rotates the result by this many degrees after the function.
- **Post Scale** (`par.Postscale`, Float x2), default `1.0`: Post transform: scales the result along x and y after the function.
- **Post Pivot** (`par.Postpivot`, Float x2), default `0.0`: Post transform pivot (x, y): the point that rotation and scale happen around.
- **Boundary** (`par.Boundary`, Float), default `0.0`: Escape radius: iteration stops once |z| exceeds this value, keeping the last value inside. 0 disables the test.
- **Borders** (`par.Borders`, Float x2), default `0.0`: Start of the soft edge for the borders output (third output), which shows the mapped image only near the edges of each repeated tile: 0.5 is the tile centre, 1 the tile edge.
- **Extend** (`par.Mode`, Menu), default `Mirror`, menu `Hold`, `Zero`, `Repeat`, `Mirror`: How the image is sampled where the warped coordinates leave 0..1: Hold the edge pixels, Zero (transparent black), Repeat the image, or Mirror it.
- **Blend** (`par.Blend`, Float), default `1.0`: Mix between the unwarped coordinates (0) and the warped ones (1).

### Common

- **Resolution** (`par.Resolution`, Int x2), default `1280`: Width and height of the built-in UV map used when nothing is wired into the input. Disabled while an input is connected; the output then takes the input resolution.
- **Input Smoothness** (`par.Inputfiltertype`, Menu), default `linear`, menu `nearest`, `linear`, `mipmap`: Filtering used when sampling the input image.
- **Viewer Smoothness** (`par.Filtertype`, Menu), default `linear`, menu `useinput`, `nearest`, `linear`, `mipmap`: Filtering used when the output is displayed at another resolution.
- **Pixel Format** (`par.Format`, Menu), default `useinput`, menu `useinput`, `rgba8fixed`, `rgba16float`, `rgba32float`, `rgb10a2fixed`, `rgba16fixed`, `rgba11float`, `mono8fixed`, `mono16fixed`, `mono16float`, `mono32float`, `rg8fixed`, `rg16fixed`, `rg16float`, `rg32float`, `a8fixed`, `a16fixed`, `a16float`, `a32float`, `monoalpha8fixed`, `monoalpha16fixed`, `monoalpha16float`, `monoalpha32float`: Pixel format of the outputs. # ConstantCHOP

A Constant CHOP with typed values: numbers, toggles, tuples, text, paths or operator references, each promoted as a property you can read and set from Python, and a snap from its input. An alternative for the Constant CHOP.

- Category: CHOPs & sensing
- Version: 1.0.5
- Access: Base
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/constantchop/

## What it does

- **Typed constants**: Every constant can be a float, integer, toggle, four-value tuple, string, file or folder path, or operator reference.
- **Channels plus a table**: Numbers, toggles and tuples come out as CHOP channels, and every constant also comes out as a DAT table of names and values.
- **Switch type without losing values**: Changing the type keeps each value wherever it converts.
- **Snap from the input**: Snap Input turns whatever is wired in into constants, one per channel, named and valued from it.
- **Replace a Constant CHOP**: Create a Constant CHOP with the alternatives shortcut held and ConstantCHOP is offered in its place.
- **Constants as properties**: Each constant is a property that reads and sets it, a _out property reads the output, and a prefix avoids clashes.

## Reach it

No global shortcut. The installer never places it into a network: its tox is in the store at `<user palette>/FNSTools/store/ConstantCHOP.tox` for the user to place by hand, and its promoted methods are called on that copy.

## Promoted API

- `Chan1` (property): The Value parameter of the block named 'chan1'; assign to set it.
- `Chan1_out` (property): The output of the block named 'chan1': the channel value for a number, else the table cell.
- `CompEditorExt` (attribute)
- `ConsumeParGroup(size: int, previous_size: int)`: Grow the sequence's block size to hold a multi-value Value parameter group of `size` components.
- `IsParGroup` (property): Returns whether the current parameter is a parameter group
- `OnAdd(block_idx: int, prev_name: str = None)`: Create, or rename, the promoted attribute pair of one block; called when a block is added or its Name changes.
- `OnPrefixChanged(old_prefix: str)`: Rebuild the promoted per-block attributes after the Prefix parameter changed from old_prefix.
- `OnTypeChanged(new_type: str)`: Rebuild every block's Value parameter in the new style (Float, Int, RGB, ...); called when the Type parameter changes.
- `OnValChanged(block_idx, _val)`: Called when a block's Value parameter changes; currently a no-op, the dependency update is disabled.
- `ParGroupChannels` (property): Returns a list of channel names for the parameter group, or an empty list if not a parameter group
- `ParGroupSize` (property): Returns the size of the parameter group, or 1 if not a parameter group
- `RefreshAllAttributes(old_prefix: str = None)`: Remove every promoted per-block attribute and create them again from the current blocks (when Promote is on).
- `SeqConst` (property): The sequence of constant blocks this tool manages (the Seqname sequence on the owner).

No commands recorded for this package.

None.

### Constant

- **Type** (`par.Type`, Menu), default `Float`, menu `Float`, `Int`, `Toggle`, `Momentary`, `XYZW`, `RGBA`, `UVW`, `WH`, `Str`, `StrMenu`, `File`, `FileSave`, `Folder`, `Python`, `Object`, `OP`, `COMP`, `PanelCOMP`, `TOP`, `TOPMulti`, `CHOP`, `SOP`, `POP`, `MAT`, `DAT`: The kind of value every constant holds. Numbers, toggles and tuples come out of the CHOP output; text, paths and operator references come out of the DAT output. Switching keeps each value where it converts.

# CookBar

Draws a bar above every operator in the network you are viewing: its cook time on top, its GPU memory below, so the expensive parts of a network stand out at a glance, with the numbers beside them if you like. A Top List in a corner names the heaviest operators and takes you to one with a click. Its toolbar button switches it on; Ctrl+right-click the button for a global Hog CHOP to stress-test against. Based on Anton Heestand's Cook Bar.

- Category: Network
- Version: 1.0.7
- Access: Free
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/cookbar/

## What it does

- **Toggle from the toolbar or quick-launch**: Click the toolbar button, run Toggle cook bar from quick-launch or switch Active on; the button lights up while the bars are on.
- **Cook time at a glance**: A bar above each operator shows its CPU plus GPU cook time, green to red up to 1 ms and growing taller past it, with stripes while it cooks.
- **GPU memory at a glance**: A bar below each operator shows the GPU memory it holds, cyan to blue up to 100 MB and growing taller up to 1 GB.
- **COMP totals**: On a COMP, the bars add up the cook time and GPU memory of everything inside it, so you can find the heavy part from the top of a project down.
- **Cooking-off marker**: A COMP whose cooking is switched off gets a grey hatched bar, so a frozen network explains itself.
- **Numeric values beside the bars**: Each bar can write its number beside it, cook time above the operator and GPU memory below.
- **Top List of the heaviest operators**: A corner list names the heaviest operators by cook time or GPU memory; click a row to select that operator and zoom to it.
- **Stress test with a Hog CHOP**: A global Hog CHOP eats part of every frame on purpose, so you can watch how the network copes; the toolbar button turns red while it runs.
- **Overlay that leaves the network untouched**: The bars draw on the shared network overlay, which leaves before every save, so display flags, annotations and operators stay as they were.

## Reach it

No global shortcut. A child of the toolkit root, reached as `op.FNS.op('CookBar')`; its promoted methods are called on that COMP.

## Promoted API

- `BarActive()`: Whether the bars are on (the Toggle cook bar chip).
- `HogActive()`: Whether the Global Hog CHOP is on (the Toggle Global Hog CHOP chip).
- `OpenHog()`: Open the Global Hog CHOP's parameters, to eat frame time on purpose while you watch the bars.
- `ToggleCookBar()`: Show or hide each operator's cook time and GPU memory above it in the network editor.
- `ToggleHog()`: Switch the Global Hog CHOP on or off.

## Commands

- **Open Global Hog CHOP** (id `openhog`): Open the Global Hog CHOP's parameters, to eat frame time on purpose while you watch the bars. Method `OpenHog`.
- **Toggle cook bar** (id `togglecookbar`): Show or hide each operator's cook time and GPU memory above it in the network editor. Method `ToggleCookBar`.
- **Toggle Global Hog CHOP** (id `togglehog`): Switch the Global Hog CHOP on or off. It DELIBERATELY eats frame time (stress test). Method `ToggleHog`.

## Hotkeys

None.

## Alternative for

None.

## Requires

- `FNS_ConfigRegistry`
- `FNS_OverlayRegistry`
- `FNS_ToolbarRegistry`

## Parameters

### CookBar

- **Active** (`par.Active`, Toggle), default `on`: Draw a bar above each operator in the network you are viewing: the top bar is its cook time (CPU + GPU, full at 1 ms), the bottom one its GPU memory. Works while the timeline plays.
- **Top List** (`par.Toplist`, Toggle), default `on`: Show a list of the viewed network's heaviest operators in a corner of the network editor while Cook Bar is on. Click a row to go there, or a tab at the top to change what it ranks by.
- **Rank By** (`par.Toprank`, Menu), default `cooktime`, menu `cooktime`, `gpumemory`: What the Top List ranks by: cook time (CPU and GPU per frame, a COMP with everything inside it) or GPU memory.
- **List Corner** (`par.Topcorner`, Menu), default `topleft`, menu `topleft`, `topright`, `bottomleft`, `bottomright`: Which corner of the network editor the Top List sits in.
- **List Margin** (`par.Topmargin`, Int), default `12`: How far the Top List sits from the edges of the network editor, and from any other tool's widget before it in the same corner, in screen points.
- **List Order** (`par.Toporder`, Int), default `100`: The Top List's place among the widgets in the same corner: lower sits nearer the corner. The Overlay tab in FNS_Hub sets it when you drag.
- **List Rows** (`par.Toprows`, Int), default `8`: How many operators the Top List shows, 1 to 12.
- **Top List Collapsed** (`par.Topcollapsed`, Toggle), default `off`: Fold the Top List to its tab row. The arrow at the right of the tabs does the same.
- **Max OPs** (`par.Maxops`, Int), default `100`: The most operators drawn at once, nearest the middle of the view first (up to 250, what the shader holds). Only operators in view count. More costs GPU time: about 0.1 ms at 50, 0.25 ms at 100 and 1.4 ms at 250 for a 1536x700 pane (measured), growing with the pane's size.
- **Values** (`par.Showvalues`, Toggle), default `off`: Write each bar's number next to it: the cook time above the operator and the GPU memory below it. Shown on operators wide enough on screen to fit them.
- **Annotation Alpha** (`par.Annotationalpha`, Float), default `0.2`: While the bars are on, the back colour of every annotation in the network you are viewing is lowered to this alpha so the bars behind it show, and put back when you leave or switch off. An annotation that is already fainter is left as it is.
- **Open Global Hog CHOP** (`par.Openhog`, Pulse): Open the parameters of the Global Hog CHOP, which eats frame time on purpose so you can watch how the network copes. Ctrl+right-click on the toolbar button does the same. The button turns red while the Hog is on.

# ExpressionPOP

Per-point attribute expressions for POPs: write lines like P = P + N * 0.1 and they compile to a GLSL compute shader, with local variables carried between lines. An alternative for the Math Combine POP.

- Category: 3D and Particles
- Version: 1.0.6
- Access: Free
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/expressionpop/

## What it does

- **Point math in plain lines**: Write one expression per line, such as `P = P + N * 0.1`, and read any point attribute of the input by its name.
- **GPU compute shader from your lines**: The lines compile into a GLSL compute shader on the GPU, so the math stays fast however many points come in.
- **Local variables**: Typed locals such as `vec3 offset = N * 0.2` carry over to every later line, so a long calculation splits into readable steps.
- **GLSL code and compile errors**: The viewer switches between the points, the generated GLSL and the compile result, and the code and the result also come out as DATs.
- **Replace a Math Combine POP**: Offered in place of a Math Combine POP, wired into the same spot, when you create one with the alternatives shortcut held.

## Reach it

No global shortcut. The installer never places it into a network: its tox is in the store at `<user palette>/FNSTools/store/ExpressionPOP.tox` for the user to place by hand, and its promoted methods are called on that copy.

## Promoted API

## Commands

- **Ready to use**: The new Select arrives selected and current, with its viewer on and a tint that marks it as a reference.
- **Undo in one step**: A single undo takes the Select away again.
- **Find them later by tag**: Every Select it makes is tagged `FNS_AltSelect`, so a Find or a `findChildren(tags=...)` sweep can list them.

## Reach it

`op.ALT_SELECT` is its global shortcut: call its promoted methods on that object from anywhere in the project.

## Promoted API

- `OnSelectOP(_op)`: Remember the newly selected operator's position, and its docked operators' positions, for the move check; called when the selection changes.
- `OnUpdate(_op: td.OP)`: Called when a watched operator changes: while the hotkey is held, a move since the selection is handed to onPosChange, which places the matching Select operator.
- `ToggleActive()`: Enable or disable AltSelect.

## Commands

- **Toggle AltSelect** (id `toggleactive`): Enable or disable AltSelect. Method `ToggleActive`.

## Hotkeys

None.

## Alternative for

None.

## Requires

- `FNS_ConfigRegistry`

## Parameters

### Custom

- **Active** (`par.Active`, Toggle), default `on`: Turn AltSelect on or off. When on, dragging a selected operator away while the modifier is held leaves a Select OP wired to the original in its place instead of moving it. Off leaves the component installed but idle.

# AutoRes

Package `FNS_AutoRes`.

Hold Alt while placing a generator TOP to have its resolution follow the project (or the panel it sits in).

- Category: Network
- Version: 3.2.11
- Access: Free
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/fns-autores/

## What it does

- **Resolution that follows the project**: A generator TOP placed with `Alt` held gets a resolution expression that follows the `parent.Project` shortcut.
- **Panel size inside panels**: Inside a panel component, such as a Container COMP, the new TOP is set to Parent Panel Size.
- **Fallback size without a Project shortcut**: Where no `parent.Project` is found, the TOP uses the resolution you set on AutoRes.
- **Default colour format**: Sets the RGB mode and the Pixel Format of the new TOP too, where it has them.
- **Skip reloads and large batches**: Leaves operators from package reloads, replicators or loading components alone, and skips a batch too large to be a drop with a Textport note.

`op.AUTO_RES` is its global shortcut: call its promoted methods on that object from anywhere in the project.

# BorderlessTD

Package `FNS_BorderlessTD`.

Borderless TouchDesigner window, plus timeline hiding.

- Category: Interface
- Version: 3.2.12
- Access: Free
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/fns-borderlesstd/

## What it does

- **Hide the title bar**: Shows and hides TouchDesigner's window title bar on one key.
- **Hide the timeline**: Shows and hides the timeline on one key.
- **Escape back to the title bar**: `Shift+Esc` always brings the title bar back, until you switch that safety net off.
- **Start borderless**: The project can open borderless, with the timeline already hidden.
- **Full screen or windowed**: Keeps a borderless window full screen, or lets it sit in a smaller window or a window zone.
- **Pause indicator**: While playback is paused, a part of TouchDesigner's UI changes colour, standing in for the hidden timeline's pause cue.
- **Hide the menu bar links**: Hide Menu Buttons removes the Wiki, Forum and Tutorials links from the menu bar.
- **Show the project name in the menu bar**: Show Project Name puts the project's file name in the menu bar, where the hidden title bar used to show it.

## Reach it

`op.FNS_BORDERLESS_TD` is its global shortcut: call its promoted methods on that object from anywhere in the project.

## Promoted API

No promoted API: the package has no extension. Its parameters, listed below, are its surface.

## Commands

- **Toggle borderless** (id `toggleborderless`): Toggle the borderless TouchDesigner main window. Method `ToggleBorderless` on `BorderlessWindow`.
- **Toggle fullscreen** (id `togglefullscreen`): Toggle fullscreen on the TouchDesigner main window. Method `ToggleFullscreen` on `BorderlessWindow`.
- **Toggle timeline** (id `toggletimeline`): Show or hide the timeline bar. Method `ToggleTimeline` on `HideTimeline`.

## Hotkeys

- `F7` (`Shortcutmakeborderless` on `FNS_BorderlessTD`)
- `alt.F7` (`Shortcut` on `FNS_BorderlessTD`)

## Alternative for

None.

## Requires

- `FNS_ConfigRegistry`
- `FNS_MainMenuRegistry`
- `FNS_ToolbarRegistry`

## Parameters

### BorderlessWindow

- **Shortcut** (`par.Shortcutmakeborderless`, Str), default `F7`: Key that shows and hides the window's title bar. Windows only.
- **Borderless State** (`par.Borderless`, Toggle), default `off`: Whether the title bar is hidden right now. Toggling this is the same as pressing the shortcut.
- **Use Shift-Esc to undo** (`par.Shiftesc`, Toggle), default `off`: Let Shift+Esc put the title bar back. Worth having while you get used to a borderless window; TouchDesigner has no window controls without one.
- **Show Project Name** (`par.Showprojectname`, Toggle), default `off`: Show the project file's name in the menu bar. Handy once the title bar, which normally carries it, is hidden.
- **Hide Menu Buttons** (`par.Hidemenubuttons`, Toggle), default `off`: Remove the Wiki, Forum and Tutorials links from the main menu bar.
- **On Start** (`par.Onstart`, Toggle), default `off`: Go borderless as soon as the project opens, rather than waiting for the shortcut.
- **Fix Fullscreen On Start** (`par.Fixfullscreenonstart`, Toggle), default `off`: Re-assert full screen shortly after the project opens. On by default because TouchDesigner does not reliably start full screen on its own.
- **Force Full Screen (always)** (`par.Fullscreen`, Toggle), default `off`: Keep the window full screen whenever it is borderless. Turn it off to run TouchDesigner borderless inside a window zone instead of over the whole display.
- **Enable** (`par.Active`, Toggle), default `off`: Turn the borderless-window feature on. Off leaves TouchDesigner's window exactly as the OS drew it and the shortcut does nothing.

### HideTimeline

- **Shortcut** (`par.Shortcut`, Str), default `alt.F7`: Key that shows and hides TouchDesigner's timeline.
- **Enable** (`par.Activetimeline`, Toggle), default `off`: Turn the timeline-hiding feature on. Off leaves the timeline alone and the shortcut does nothing.
- **Hide Timeline** (`par.Statetimeline`, Toggle), default `off`: Whether the timeline is hidden right now. Toggling this is the same as pressing the shortcut.
- **State on Startup** (`par.Stateonstartuptimeline`, Toggle), default `off`: Whether the timeline starts hidden when the project opens.

# ColorUI

Package `FNS_ColorUI`.

Operator and family colour palettes, with the active palette roaming through config.

- Category: Interface
- Version: 3.2.12
- Access: Free
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/fns-colorui/

## What it does

- **Recolour UI elements**: Every colour in TouchDesigner's interface in one list, each with its default and a reset.
- **Operator family colours**: Recolour whole operator families, POPs included.
- **Save and reapply your colours**: Your colours are stored in the component, applied as the project opens, and follow you to other projects and through updates.
- **Filter the list**: Narrow the list by name with wildcards, to changed colours only, or to colours close to a reference colour.
- **Change many at once**: Give one colour to everything listed, or to a whole group, and reset a group in one go.
- **Randomize and undo**: Throw random colours at the whole interface, then put your own colours back with one click.
- **Share your colours as JSON**: Export writes only the colours you changed to a JSON file, to keep with a project, commit or send to someone.
- **Import a JSON palette**: Import applies such a file; its colours take precedence over the ones stored locally, and elements this build does not know are skipped.
- **Open from Hub or quick-launch**: The colour editor opens from the OpColor tab of Hub (the FNS button in the main-menu bar), Open color UI in quick-launch, or Open UI on the component.
- **Console tab in the browser**: With Expose to Console on, the same editor is served in the browser as the ColorUI tab of Console, the toolkit's web front.

## Reach it

`op.FNS_COLOR_UI` is its global shortcut: call its promoted methods on that object from anywhere in the project.

## Promoted API

- `ApplyOverrides()`: Write every stored override into ui.colors.
- `ConsoleCommand(msg)`: One page->TD message, same vocabulary as the title bridge (_dispatch), answered with the resulting state plus any toasts the command raised.
- `ConsoleState()`: The page state as the console tab's HTTP answer: {'ok', 'state'}.
- `DoExport(dialog=False)`: Save the stored overrides as JSON to the File parameter's path, or one chosen in a dialog.
- `DoImport(dialog=False)`: Load UI colors from the JSON file the File parameter names, or one chosen in a dialog, and apply them.
- `ExportPalette()`: Export the current UI colors to file.
- `ImportPalette()`: Import a UI color palette from file.
- `OnBrowserTitle(raw)`: Called by watch_browser when the page rewrites document.title.
- `OnConsoleExposure(exposed)`: FNS_Console hand-off: the host calls this instead of flipping the renderer itself, so the viewer rule above stays the single owner.
- `OnHubExposure(exposed)`: FNS_Hub hand-off: our panel is the hub's OpColor tab; the hub calls this as the tab is shown/hidden.
- `OnStart()`: Project start (execute1 onStart/onCreate).
- `OpenColorUI()`: Open the TouchDesigner UI color editor.
- `OpenUI()`: Served by the console: open its ColorUI tab.
- `Overrides` (property): The UI color overrides this tool stores on its COMP, element name to RGB.
- `Randomize()`: Give every UI color a random value (UndoRandom takes it back).
- `RandomizeColors()`: Randomize the UI colors.
- `ResetAll()`: Reset every UI color to TouchDesigner's defaults and drop the stored overrides.
- `ResetAllColors()`: Reset every UI color to its default.
- `SendState()`: Push the current color state to the page in the in-TD browser.
- `SyncLocalBrowser()`: The local Web Render runs only while someone can see it: the viewer is open AND the console is not serving the page.
- `Toast(text)`: Show a short message on the page; a console request in flight collects it for its answer.
- `UndoRandom()`: Undo Randomize: TouchDesigner's defaults with the stored overrides applied again.
- `UndoRandomize()`: Undo the last color randomization.

## Commands

- **Export color palette** (id `exportpalette`): Export the current UI colors to file. Method `ExportPalette`.
- **Import color palette** (id `importpalette`): Import a UI color palette from file. Method `ImportPalette`.
- **Open color UI** (id `opencolorui`): Open the TouchDesigner UI color editor. Method `OpenColorUI`.
- **Randomize colors** (id `randomizecolors`): Randomize the UI colors. Method `RandomizeColors`.
- **Reset all colors** (id `resetallcolors`): Reset every UI color to its default. Method `ResetAllColors`.
- **Undo randomize** (id `undorandomize`): Undo the last color randomization. Method `UndoRandomize`.

## Hotkeys

None.

## Alternative for

None.

## Requires

- `FNS_ConfigRegistry`
- `FNS_Console`
- `FNS_HubRegistry`

## Parameters

### ColorUI

- **Open UI** (`par.Openui`, Pulse): Open the colour editor. It is also the OpColor tab of FNS_Hub, and, with Expose on the Registry page, a tab of FNS_Console in the browser.
- **File (.json)** (`par.File`, FileSave): Where Export writes and Import reads. A .json file you can keep in a project, commit, or hand to someone else.
- **Import** (`par.Import`, Pulse): Read colours from the file above and apply them. Imported colours take precedence over the ones saved locally in the component.
- **Export** (`par.Export`, Pulse): Write the current colours to the file above, so they can be shared or version-controlled.
- **Auto-Load Colors** (`par.Autoload`, Toggle), default `on`: Apply the colours saved in this component when the project opens. Off leaves TouchDesigner's own colours until you open the UI and apply.
- **Group By** (`par.Groupby`, Menu), default `prefix`, menu `prefix`, `role`: How the editor's list is organised: Prefix groups elements by the name they start with, Role groups them by what they are used for.

# CommandKit

Package `FNS_CommandKit`.

Drop-in kit that lets ANY component publish quick-launch commands to the in-TouchDesigner command palette and the TDX launcher: decorate a promoted method, or declare a spec. Guarded: with no registry in the session nothing happens and nothing errors.

- Category: Developer
- Version: 3.2.6
- Access: Free
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/fns-commandkit/

## What it does

- **Publish commands from any component**: Drop the kit in as a direct child and the methods you mark appear in the CommandPalette and the TDXL launcher.
- **Safe without a registry**: With no command registry in the session nothing happens and nothing errors, so the component works the same for people without the palette.
- **Decorator for command methods**: The fns_command decorator derives label, help and prompted parameters from the method name, docstring and signature; Literal hints become menus.
- **Context, state and identity options**: Decorator extras set a context for greying out, a live state chip, surface, capability, hidden, and a canonical identity shared across packages.
- **Declare commands without imports**: Promote an FnsCommands() method that returns a spec list, with no imports at all: id, label, method, help, prompted params and every decorator extra as plain dict keys.
- **Announces on load**: Once the component declares a command the kit tags it and registers it, so a registry that arrives later still finds it; nothing to unregister.
- **Check that commands arrived**: Three reads tell you whether your commands are served, and a short ladder says what to look at when one is missing.
- **Announce again after changes**: Call Announce() to republish the component after its command set changes at runtime.
- **Tell placed copies apart**: Promote FnsInstance() and FnsToolName() so palettes distinguish multiple copies and favourites reach all of them (FNS_CommandRegistry 3.2.1 or newer).

## Reach it

No global shortcut. A child of the toolkit root, reached as `op.FNS.op('FNS_CommandKit')`; its promoted methods are called on that COMP.

## Promoted API

- `Announce()`: Re-register the hosting tool's commands (after changing them).

## Commands

No commands recorded for this package.

## Hotkeys

None.

## Alternative for

None.

## Requires

Nothing.

## Parameters

None.

# CommandPalette

Package `FNS_CommandPalette`.

A command palette inside TouchDesigner: every command your FNS tools declare and TouchDesigner's own palette components in one ranked list, opened with a hotkey and aware of what you are looking at. Manage favourites and hidden commands from its tab in Hub.

- Category: Interface
- Version: 3.2.18
- Access: Free
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/fns-commandpalette/

## What it does

- **Find any command on one key**: Opens over the network you are in with every command your FNS tools declare, TouchDesigner's built-in commands and its palette components in one ranked list.
- **Context-aware ranking**: Commands about the parameter under your mouse, the selected operator or the current network come first.
- **Typo-tolerant search**: Initials, typos, letters in order and British or American spellings all find a command, with strict matches ranked first.
- **Search by what a command does**: A word from a command's help or its tool's documentation finds it, so `copy` finds PasteFromClipboard, and the row says why it matched.
- **Actions first for words like copy**: A word that starts command titles, such as copy, open or reset, lists the commands that start with it first, then components named with it.
- **Scoping prefixes**: A leading character narrows the list to commands, tool commands, components or one tool's commands.
- **Navigate the network**: `/` is the root, `./` where you came from and each `..` a level up; Right drills into a row and Left backs out.
- **Step through a command's values**: A command that takes values asks for them one at a time: a menu as pick rows, anything else as a field naming its type and default.
- **Presets that run on Enter**: `Alt+S` saves a command with its values as a preset row, which runs on Enter without prompting.
- **Place palette components**: TouchDesigner's palette components, your own folders included, land on your mouse ready to place, or drag into any pane.
- **Stars and hidden commands**: Star commands with `Ctrl+D` to lead their tier, and hide the ones you never use with `Ctrl+H`.
- **Rank by usage**: Commands you run often rank higher, the lift fading over a couple of weeks unused; Rank By Usage switches it off.
- **Query history**: `Alt+Up` and `Alt+Down` cycle through the queries you have run before.
- **Commands tab in Hub**: Every registered command, hidden ones included, with Star and Hidden toggles shared with TDX Launcher Ultra.
- **Install from the palette**: A tool you can install but have not yet shows as an Install row; Enter installs it.
- **Call extension methods**: `~` lists the public methods of a COMP's extensions and calls them with the arguments you type.

## Reach it

No global shortcut. A child of the toolkit root, reached as `op.FNS.op('FNS_CommandPalette')`; its promoted methods are called on that COMP.

## Promoted API

- `Activate(row: dict, args: dict = None)`: Enter on a row.
- `ActivateSelected()`: Enter.
- `CaptureContext()`: Snapshot what the user is looking at, BEFORE the window opens.
- `Catalogue(rebuild: bool = False)`: Every row the palette can offer, commands first.
- `Choose(onChosen, title: str = None)`: Open the palette as a picker: Enter or a click on a command or a preset hands it to onChosen instead of running it, as a dict {'key', 'label', 'kwargs'}; closing without a pick calls onChosen(None).
- `ClearUsage()`: Forget this palette's usage history.
- `Context()`: The active snapshot, capturing one now if the palette never opened.
- `DeletePreset(preset_id: str)`: Remove a saved preset by id; False when there is none.
- `Dismiss()`: Close the palette and stop listening for keys.
- `Favourites()`: Identities (tool#id) starred with Ctrl+D here or in the launcher.
- `History()`: Executed queries, oldest first.
- `IsHidden(key: str)`: Whether a command is hidden from the palette's listing, by the user's override or the tool's own default.
- `IsOpen()`: Whether the palette window is open right now.
- `ListPresets()`: Every saved preset: label, target command and baked arguments.
- `OnHubExposure(exposed: bool)`: FNS_Hub tells a tab's component when it is shown; rebuild then.
- `OnInputBlur()`: The input lost keyboard focus (panel/input_callbacks onFocusEnd).
- `OnKey(key, ctrl=False, alt=False, shift=False)`: Raw key names from the Keyboard In DAT while the palette is open.
- `OnManagerButton(name: str)`: The toolbar buttons on the Commands tab.
- `OnQuery(text)`: Every keystroke in the input lands here (editablecontinuous).
- `OnRowClick(index: int)`: A mouse click on a row (panel/panelexec_rows): select it, then do exactly what Enter does, so clicks and keys can never diverge.
- `Rank(query: str = '', limit: int = None)`: The rows to show, best first.
- `RefreshManager()`: Rebuild the Commands tab's table: every registry command, hidden ones included, with the star and hidden state from the prefs.
- `SavePreset(ident: str, args: dict, label: str)`: Add a preset over the command with identity `ident` (tool#id), `args` baked in.
- `Summon()`: Open the palette over whatever the user is looking at right now.
- `ToggleFavourite(key: str)`: Flip a command's favourite flag in the curation; returns the new state.
- `ToggleHidden(key: str)`: Flip a command's visibility.
- `UsageBonus(key: str)`: The current ranking bonus (0..8) for a command identity, tool#id.

## Commands

No commands recorded for this package.

## Hotkeys

- `ctrl.shift.p` (`Hotkey` on `FNS_CommandPalette`)

## Alternative for

None.

## Requires

- `FNS_ConfigRegistry`
- `FNS_HubRegistry`

## Parameters

### Palette

- **Hotkey** (`par.Hotkey`, Str), default `ctrl.shift.p`: Keyboard shortcut that opens the palette. Space-separated combos, parts joined with a dot, e.g. ctrl.shift.p. Rebind it from FNS_HotkeyManager.
- **Justify and Offset To...** (`par.Justifyoffsetto`, Menu), default `specifydisplay`, menu `primarydisplay`, `specifydisplay`, `alldisplays`: Which display the palette window is placed on: the primary one, the one set on the window, or the bounds of all displays.
- **Ignore Taskbar** (`par.Ignoretaskbar`, Toggle), default `on`: Place the palette as if the taskbar were not there.
- **DPI Scaling** (`par.Dpiscaling`, Menu), default `usedpiscale`, menu `native`, `usedpiscale`: Size the palette in native pixels, or scaled with the display DPI.
- **Shift to Single Display** (`par.Single`, Menu), default `off`, menu `off`, `singledisplay`, `cursordisplay`: Keep the palette on one display: off, on a single display, or on the display with the cursor.
- **Favourite keys** (`par.Favouritekeys`, Str), default `[]`: Legacy store of starred command identities (tool#id) from before the shared curation file; adopted into that file on first read, then emptied.
- **Query history** (`par.Queryhistory`, Str), default `[]`: JSON list of executed palette queries, oldest first, recalled with Alt+Up / Alt+Down. Persisted by the config host.
- **Visibility overrides** (`par.Visibilityoverrides`, Str), default `{}`: Legacy store of visibility overrides (tool#id -> hidden or shown) from before the shared curation file; adopted into that file on first read, then emptied.
- **Presets** (`par.Presets`, Str), default `[]`: Legacy store of presets from before the shared curation file; adopted into that file on first read, then emptied.
- **Rank By Usage** (`par.Rankbyusage`, Toggle), default `on`: Commands you run often rank higher: a small bonus that fades with a 14-day half-life and breaks ties between similar matches, never above a better match or a favourite. Usage is shared with the TDXLU launcher (command-usage.json) and recorded even when this is off.

# CommandRegistry

Package `FNS_CommandRegistry`.

Collects the commands your tools declare and serves them to whatever can run them: the in-TouchDesigner command palette and the TDX launcher. Discovery is by tag, so a tool installed before any consumer still appears the moment one arrives.

- Category: Core
- Version: 3.2.11
- Access: Free
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/fns-commandregistry/

## What it does

- **Share one list across palettes**: The CommandPalette and TDX Launcher Ultra read the same commands, and favourites, hidden commands and presets made in one show in the other.
- **Tag-based tool discovery**: Finds tools tagged fnscommands and harvests their commands, so a tool installed before any palette or launcher still appears when one arrives.
- **Curation that survives moves**: Favourites, hidden flags and presets are keyed on tool name and command id, so they survive a tool being moved in the network.
- **Presets per copy or pinned**: A preset runs on every copy of a tool, or is pinned to one instance label and waits quietly where no copy carries it.
- **Built-in TouchDesigner commands**: Serves TouchDesigner's own actions, such as the Textport, dialogs, pane changes, saving, recent files, realtime, perform mode and cook rate, badged TD in the palette.
- **Newest version wins for duplicates**: When two packages offer the same canonical command, the newest package version is served and the other set aside, so the list never doubles.
- **Tools work without it**: Every call a tool makes is guarded, so with no registry in the session nothing happens and nothing errors.
- **Commands derived from methods**: Builds each command's label, help and prompted parameters from the method's name, docstring and signature, with type hints setting input styles.
- **Declared context, surface and state**: Tools declare what a command acts on, where it is offered, where its live value lives, its capability group and a cross-package canonical id.
- **Commands for each tool copy**: Each copy of a multi-copy tool registers its commands under its own path, labelled by FnsInstance() and grouped under one name by FnsToolName().
- **Declaration validation**: Enforces limits at harvest (24 commands per tool, 6 parameters, 5 contexts, 8 surfaces) and rejects malformed declarations with a reason.
- **Consumer API**: Commands(), Run(key, args), RescanTools(), Shadowed(), Rev() and Version() let a palette or launcher list, run and re-harvest commands and check the contract version.

## Reach it

A registry. `op.FNS_COMMANDREGISTRY` is its global shortcut, promoted into /sys/FNS_Registries while the toolkit runs: call its promoted methods on that object from anywhere in the project, never on the master inside the toolkit root. See registries.md.

## Promoted API

- `Commands()`: Flat wire-ready list; prunes registrations whose tool is gone.
- `Register(owner, commands=None)`: Replace OWNER's registered command set.
- `Repromote()`: Dev helper: replace the /sys global with a fresh copy of THIS shipper, migrating registrations — regardless of version.
- `RescanTools()`: Collect commands from every COMP tagged TOOL_TAG: its promoted FnsCommands() spec list when it has one, else its decorated (`_fns_command`-marked) methods.
- `Rev()`: Monotonic change counter - bumps on every registry mutation.
- `Run(key, args=None, kwargs=None)`: Execute one registered command by key ('<owner path>#<id>').
- `Shadowed()`: Commands withheld because another package won their canonical id.
- `Unregister(owner)`: Drop OWNER's commands (COMP or path).
- `Version()`: This instance's registry version (family version-compare).

## Commands

- **Add Embody** (id `addembody`): Download the latest Embody release and add it to the project root. Method `AddEmbody` on `FNS_BuiltinCommands/TD_Components`.
- **Add TDX Launcher Utility** (id `addlauncherutility`): Download the latest TDX Launcher Utility and add it to the project root. Method `AddLauncherUtility` on `FNS_BuiltinCommands/TD_Components`.

- **Open Beat** (id `openbeat`): Open the beat / tap-tempo dialog. Method `OpenBeat` on `FNS_BuiltinCommands/TD_Dialogs`.
- **Open Bookmarks** (id `openbookmarks`): Open the Bookmarks dialog. Method `OpenBookmarks` on `FNS_BuiltinCommands/TD_Dialogs`.

- **Open Performance Monitor** (id `openperformancemonitor`): Open the Performance Monitor. Method `OpenPerformanceMonitor` on `FNS_BuiltinCommands/TD_Dialogs`.

- **Customize parent** (id `customizeparent`): Open the Component Editor on the component whose network you are in, to add custom parameters. Method `CustomizeParent` on `FNS_BuiltinCommands/TD_Session`.
- **Load recent file** (id `loadrecent`): Load a File > Recent entry (1 = most recent). CLOSES this project. Method `LoadRecent` on `FNS_BuiltinCommands/TD_Session`. Params: `index: int = 1`.
