# LayerSep3D

Slices an image into depth layers by a channel threshold and instances them as a stack in 3D, with per layer threshold, softness, mix, position, scale and rotation driven by curves or CHOPs.

- Category: 3D and Particles
- Version: 1.0.4
- Access: Base
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/layersep3d/

## What it does

- **Slice an image into layers**: Each layer takes the part of the image that passes its threshold on the channel you pick, with a soft edge to its neighbours.
- **Instance the layers as a 3D stack**: The layers are instanced as planes along Z in one Geometry COMP, so a camera pointed at it sees a flat picture with depth.
- **Shape each value with a curve**: Threshold, softness, mix, depth, scale and rotation each follow a curve over the layers, set by offset, amplitude, power and phase.
- **Shuffle the layer order**: Reverse, repeat, phase-shift or randomise which layer each plane shows, or show one layer on every plane.
- **Drive layers from CHOPs**: CHOPs with one sample per layer take over the threshold, softness or mix curves.
- **Instancing overrides**: Per-layer Z, scale and rotation can also be overridden in the instancing.
- **Colour the layers from another image**: Slice one image and draw another on the layers, such as a depth map cutting up the camera feed it came from.
- **Output the layers as a texture**: out_layers gives the layer stack as a 2D texture array or 3D texture for your own instancing.

## Reach it

No global shortcut. Place a copy: it is the FNS operator family member `layerSep3D` (Layer Sep 3D) on the FNS tab of the OP Create dialog, also at `<user palette>/FNSTools/FNS/LayerSep3D.tox`. Its promoted methods are called on the placed copy.

## Promoted API

No promoted API: the package has no extension. Its parameters, listed below, are its surface.

## Commands

No commands recorded for this package.

## Hotkeys

None.

## Alternative for

None.

## Requires

Nothing.

## Parameters

### Custom

- **Layers** (`par.Layers`, Int), default `10`: Number of layers the input is split into (the depth of the output texture and the number of instanced quads). The threshold range is divided into this many equal bands, one per layer. Minimum 2.
- **Reverse Layer Order** (`par.Reverse`, Toggle), default `off`: Flips the order of the layers in the output texture: layer 0 becomes the brightest band instead of the darkest.
- **Open Material** (`par.Open`, Pulse): Opens the parameter dialog of the material the layers are rendered with.
- **Mode** (`par.Mode`, Menu), default `luminanc`, menu `luminanc`, `red`, `green`, `blue`, `alpha`, `rgbavg`, `rgbaavg`, `rgbmax`, `rgbamax`, `rgbmin`, `rgbamin`: Which value of the mask pixel is compared against the thresholds: luminance, a single channel, or an average, maximum or minimum of the channels.
- **Threshold Offset** (`par.Thoffs`, Float), default `0.0`: Added to every layer threshold before the range mapping. Positive values push all band edges up.
- **Threshold Amplitude** (`par.Thamp`, Float), default `1.0`: Scales the spread of the thresholds. 1 spreads the bands over the whole range, smaller values squeeze them toward the bottom, negative values reverse the ramp.
- **Threshold Range** (`par.Thrange`, Float x2), default `0.0`: Mask values (min, max) the layers are spread across. The range is split into Layers equal bands: the first layer also takes everything below the range, the last layer everything above its lower edge.
- **Threshold Power** (`par.Threshpow`, Float), default `1.0`: Exponent applied to the threshold ramp. 1 = equal bands, above 1 = thinner bands at the bottom, below 1 = thinner bands at the top.
- **Threshold Phase** (`par.Thphase`, Float), default `0.0`: Rotates the threshold ramp across the layers (0 to 1), so the band order wraps around.
- **Threshold CHOP (override)** (`par.Threshold`, CHOP), default `None`: Optional CHOP with one sample per layer that replaces the generated thresholds. Leave empty to use the Threshold parameters above (a CHOP wired to the threshold input also overrides them).
- **Softness Offset** (`par.Softoffset`, Float), default `0.0`: Softness added to every layer edge. Softness is the width of the blend between neighbouring layers, in mask units.
- **Softness Amplitude** (`par.Softamp`, Float), default `0.0`: How much the softness ramps across the layers, from 0 at the first layer to this value at the last.
- **Softness Power** (`par.Softpow`, Float), default `1.0`: Exponent applied to the softness ramp across the layers.
- **Softness Phase** (`par.Softphase`, Float), default `0.0`: Rotates the softness ramp across the layers (0 to 1).
- **Softness CHOP (override)** (`par.Softness`, CHOP), default `None`: Optional CHOP with one sample per layer that replaces the generated softness values.
- **Mix Amplitude** (`par.Mixamp`, Float), default `0.0`: How much of the content above each layer is left in it, ramped across the layers. 0 = each layer holds only its own band.
- **Mix Offset** (`par.Mixoffset`, Float), default `0.0`: Mix added to every layer. 1 keeps everything from the layer upward in each slice.
- **Mix Power** (`par.Mixpow`, Float), default `1.0`: Exponent applied to the mix ramp across the layers.
- **Mix Phase** (`par.Mixphase`, Float), default `0.0`: Rotates the mix ramp across the layers (0 to 1).
- **Mix CHOP (override)** (`par.Mix`, CHOP), default `None`: Optional CHOP with one sample per layer that replaces the generated mix values.
- **Texture Index** (`par.Lookupindex`, Header)
- **Invert Texture Index** (`par.Invert2`, Float), default `0.0`: Blends the texture index each quad samples from normal (0) to reversed (1), so the quad order and the layer order can run against each other.
- **Texture Index Phase** (`par.Phase`, Float), default `0.0`: Shifts which layer each instanced quad samples, as a phase of the index ramp.
- **Texture Index Exponent** (`par.Expval`, Float), default `1.0`: Exponent applied to the texture index ramp. 1 = one layer per quad in order; other values bunch the layers toward one end.
- **Texture Index Period** (`par.Period`, Float), default `1.0`: Period of the texture index ramp across the quads. 1 = each layer once; smaller values repeat the layer sequence.
- **Randomize Seed** (`par.Randomize`, Float), default `0.0`: When above 0, shuffles which layer each quad samples, using this value as the seed. 0 = no shuffle.
- **Single Layer** (`par.Single`, Toggle), default `off`: Every quad samples the same layer, chosen by Select.
- **Select Layer** (`par.Select`, Float), default `0.0`: The layer every quad shows while Single Layer is on (0 = first layer).

### Transform

- **These can be overridden in the instancing...** (`par.Thesecanbeoverriddenintheinstancing`, Header)
- **Z Offset** (`par.Tzoffset`, Float), default `0.0`: Z position added to every quad.
- **Z Amplitude** (`par.Tzamplitude`, Float), default `1.0`: Total Z spread of the quads, from the first layer to the last.
- **Z Power** (`par.Tzpow`, Float), default `1.0`: Exponent applied to the Z spread, so the quads bunch toward the front or the back.
- **Z Phase** (`par.Tzphase`, Float), default `0.0`: Rotates the Z ramp across the quads (0 to 1).
- **Scale Offset** (`par.Scaleoffset`, Float), default `1.0`: Uniform scale of every quad (1 = original size).

# LinkOPs

Links the parameters of several operators so a change on one lands on all of them, with exceptions by operator and by parameter, an automatic mode and a one-shot sync.

- Category: Parameters
- Version: 1.0.4
- Access: Base
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/linkops/

## What it does

- **Link operators by pattern**: Name the operators with patterns such as `noise*` or `level1 level2`, and a parameter changed on one is written to the others.
- **Link expressions and modes**: Values follow, and by default so do expressions and parameter modes.
- **Exclude operators and parameters**: Leave out operators that match the pattern anyway, and parameters such as `t? seed` to keep transforms and seeds independent.
- **Constant-only linking**: Link only parameters in constant mode on both sides, so an expression on one operator is never overwritten.
- **Auto-update the operator list**: With Auto on, the list follows operators as they are added, renamed or removed.
- **Sync on demand**: Operators added later join when you press Sync.
- **Match parameters by name across types**: Operators of different types can share a link; the parameters they have in common by name are kept in step.

## Reach it

No global shortcut. Place a copy: it is the FNS operator family member `linkOPs` (Link OPs) on the FNS tab of the OP Create dialog, also at `<user palette>/FNSTools/FNS/LinkOPs.tox`. Its promoted methods are called on the placed copy.

## Promoted API

No promoted API: the package has no extension. Its parameters, listed below, are its surface.

## Commands

No commands recorded for this package.

## Hotkeys

None.

## Alternative for

None.

## Requires

Nothing.

## Parameters

### Custom

- **Active** (`par.Active`, Toggle), default `on`: Master switch. When off, parameter changes are no longer propagated between the linked operators.
- **OPs** (`par.Ops`, Str): Space-separated operator name patterns (wildcards allowed, e.g. noise* level1) to link, searched in the network LinkOPs sits in.
- **Except** (`par.Except`, Str): Space-separated operator name patterns to leave out of the link even when they match Ops.
- **Par Except** (`par.Parexcept`, Str): Space-separated parameter name patterns (e.g. t? seed) that are never propagated.
- **Auto** (`par.Auto`, Toggle), default `off`: Keep the list of linked operators up to date automatically as operators are added, renamed or removed.
- **Sync** (`par.Sync`, Pulse): Rescan the network for operators matching Ops now. Use this when Auto is off.
- **Constant Only** (`par.Constantonly`, Toggle), default `off`: Only propagate between parameters that are in constant mode on both sides; expressions, exports and binds are left alone.

# MaskDraw

Draw a mask with the mouse straight onto the image: a panel you paint in, with the mask and the masked image as outputs, a lock and a reset.

- Category: Visual
- Version: 1.0.6
- Access: Pro
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/maskdraw/

## What it does

- **Paint and erase on the image**: Paint on the input image with the left button and erase with the right; the panel follows the input's aspect.
- **Output the mask and the masked image**: Outputs the drawn mask and the input inside the painted area, to key a composite, drive a Level or mark a projection surface.
- **Reset the mask**: Middle-click in the panel clears the mask, and so does Reset, which keeps it clear while it is on.
- **Show or hide the button bar**: Ctrl and middle-click shows or hides the button bar, and Show Input, Show Mask and Show Brush choose what the panel draws.
- **Lock a finished mask**: Lock keeps a finished mask from being changed by a stray click or reset.
- **Pause drawing**: Switching Active off hides the brush and ignores the mouse, and the mask stays as it is.
- **Save the mask with the project**: Optionally bakes the mask into the component on every save, so it is back when the project reopens.

## Reach it

No global shortcut. Place a copy: it is the FNS operator family member `maskDraw` (Mask Draw) on the FNS tab of the OP Create dialog, also at `<user palette>/FNSTools/FNS/MaskDraw.tox`. Its promoted methods are called on the placed copy.

None.

- **Show Input** (`par.Showinput`, Toggle), default `off`: Shows the input image in the display panel behind the mask. Off shows the input only inside the painted area.

Off (default): the mask lives only in the session and nothing is written into the file.

# MoveDetectDir

Reads which way things move in a camera or any image with optical flow and turns it into left/right and down/up channels, with thresholds, inversion and filtering, for swipe and gesture triggers.

- Category: CHOPs & sensing
- Version: 1.0.5
- Access: Base
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/movedetectdir/

## What it does

- **Optical flow direction**: Runs optical flow on the input image and measures how much of the flow points left, right, down and up.
- **Direction channels**: Outputs LR and DU channels that swing toward the direction of movement once it passes a threshold, for swipe and gesture triggers.
- **Filter out noise and small motion**: Blur on the input, a flow threshold and a movement threshold per axis keep camera noise and small motion from firing it.
- **Invert a direction for mirrored cameras**: Flips either direction for a mirrored camera.
- **Smooth the channels**: Smooths the direction channels over a time you set.

## Reach it

No global shortcut. Place a copy: it is the FNS operator family member `moveDetectDir` (Move Detect Dir) on the FNS tab of the OP Create dialog, also at `<user palette>/FNSTools/FNS/MoveDetectDir.tox`. Its promoted methods are called on the placed copy.

## Promoted API

No promoted API: the package has no extension. Its parameters, listed below, are its surface.

## Commands

No commands recorded for this package.

## Hotkeys

None.

## Alternative for

None.

## Requires

Nothing.

## Parameters

### Custom

- **Input Filter Size** (`par.Size`, Int), default `7`: Blur applied to the input before the optical flow, in pixels. More blur ignores small noise.
- **Optflow Lambda** (`par.Lambda`, Float), default `0.1`: Smoothing of the optical flow: higher values give a steadier, less detailed flow.
- **OptFlow Threshold** (`par.Threshold`, Float), default `0.0`: The smallest flow that counts as movement; weaker flow is ignored.
- **Move Threshold X** (`par.Movethresholdx`, Float), default `300.0`: How much horizontal movement it takes before LR swings left or right.
- **Move Threshold Y** (`par.Movethresholdy`, Float), default `300.0`: How much vertical movement it takes before DU swings down or up.
- **Inverse X** (`par.Inversex`, Toggle), default `off`: Flip the left/right direction, for a mirrored camera.
- **Inverse Y** (`par.Inversey`, Toggle), default `off`: Flip the down/up direction.
- **Filter Width** (`par.Width`, Float), default `0.2`: How long the output channels are smoothed over, in seconds.

# Particles2D_POP

A 2D particle simulation as a POP loop: a source image emits particles, curl noise and wind effectors steer them with lookup ranges, trails stretch them, and the loop rides out as points for your own render.

- Category: 3D and Particles
- Version: 1.0.6
- Access: Base
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/particles2d-pop/

## What it does

- **Emit from a source image**: Particles are born from the image on in_source and carry its colours, each with its own life, mass and drag.
- **Curl noise field**: A moving curl noise field swirls the particles, with its strength set per axis and its speed on the Curl page.
- **Wind with variance**: A wind blows the particles along a direction you set, with random variance on top; it starts at zero.
- **Steer forces with images**: Each force reads an image through its own lookup, so a picture or a mask decides where it is strong and where it is off.
- **Motion trails**: Trails stretch the points along their motion.
- **Points out for your own render**: The simulated points come out of out_loopout, ready for a Render TOP with your own material or any POP that takes points.
- **Insert your own POPs into the loop**: out_loopout and in_loopin are the two ends of the simulation loop, so POPs of your own can sit inside it.

No global shortcut. Place a copy: it is the FNS operator family member `particles2D` (Particles 2D) on the FNS tab of the OP Create dialog, also at `<user palette>/FNSTools/FNS/Particles2D_POP.tox`. Its promoted methods are called on the placed copy.

# ParticlesGpuUltimate

A GPU particle system driven by images: a thresholded source emits particles, and look, life, turbulence, wind and force fields shape them, each optionally read from its own image, with a feedback pass for trails and one rendered output.

- Category: 3D and Particles
- Version: 2.0.4
- Access: Pro
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/particlesgpuultimate/

## What it does

- **Emit particles from an image**: The source image is thresholded to decide where particles are born and what colour they carry.
- **Material and particle shape**: Pick the material, the SOP shape for each particle and the maximum particle size on the Look page.
- **Fade particles over their life**: Set how long particles live, fade them in and out at either end of their life, and shrink or dim them as they age.
- **Turbulence and wind**: Turbulence and wind act differently on the dark and the bright parts of an image, so a picture decides where particles swirl or drift.
- **Steer each effector with its own image**: Life, turbulence and wind can each read their own image, apart from the one that emits the particles.
- **Force fields you place**: Radial, axial, vortex and spiral fields that you place, each with its own reach and strength.
- **Feedback trails**: A feedback pass draws trails behind the particles, mixed in with Dry / Wet, over the source or a background colour.
- **Replace the position and colour maps**: Position and colour maps of your own replace the ones derived from the source image.
- **Optical flow movement**: An optical-flow map pushes the particles, as hard as Optical Flow Magnitude sets.

## Reach it

No global shortcut. Place a copy: it is the FNS operator family member `particlesGpuUltimate` (Particles GPU Ultimate) on the FNS tab of the OP Create dialog, also at `<user palette>/FNSTools/FNS/ParticlesGpuUltimate.tox`. Its promoted methods are called on the placed copy.

## Promoted API

No promoted API: the package has no extension. Its parameters, listed below, are its surface.

No commands recorded for this package.

None.

None.

## Requires

Nothing.

## Parameters

### Source

- **Source Res** (`par.Sourceres`, XYZW x2), default `0.0`: Resolution the source image is sampled at.
- **Interpolate Source Point Position** (`par.Interpolatepoint`, Toggle), default `on`: When using a low resolution source object, toggling this parameter will spawn particles from interpolated positions of the original source.
- **Source Thresh** (`par.Sourcethresh`, Header)
- **Comparator** (`par.Comparator`, Menu), default `less`, menu `less`, `greater`, `lessorequal`, `greaterorequal`, `equal`, `notequal`: How pixels are compared with the threshold to decide where particles are born.
- **RGB** (`par.Rgb2`, Menu), default `luminance`, menu `luminance`, `red`, `green`, `blue`, `alpha`, `rgbaverage`, `average`, `rgbmax`, `max`: Which channel of the source image is compared with Source Threshold.
- **Source Threshold** (`par.Sourcethreshold`, Float), default `0.5`: The brightness a pixel needs, by the comparator, to emit particles.
- **Source Mix** (`par.Sourcemix`, Header)
- **OverUnderLay Source** (`par.Menu`, Menu), default `Input`, menu `Input`, `Thresholded`: What is composited with the particles: the input image or the thresholded source.
- **Under Opac** (`par.Sourceunderopac`, Float), default `1.0`: Opacity of the source image underneath the particles.
- **Operation** (`par.Operand`, Menu), default `multiply`, menu `add`, `atop`, `average`, `brightest`, `burncolor`, `burnlinear`, `chromadifference`, `color`, `darkercolor`, `difference`, `dimmest`, `divide`, `dodge`, `exclude`, `freeze`, `glow`, `hardlight`, `hardmix`, `heat`, `hue`, `inside`, `insideluminance`, `inverse`, `lightercolor`, `luminancedifference`, `maximum`, `minimum`, `multiply`, `negate`, `outside`, `outsideluminance`, `over`, `overlay`, `pinlight`, `reflect`, `screen`, `softlight`, `linearlight`, `stencilluminance`, `subtract`, `subtractive`, `under`, `vividlight`, `xor`, `yfilm`, `zfilm`: How the source and the particles are composited.
- **Opac** (`par.Opacity2`, Float), default `1.0`: Opacity of the composited source.
- **Comp Over Background Color** (`par.Compover`, Toggle), default `off`: Composite the result over the background colour.

### pGpu

- **Render Res** (`par.Res`, XYZW x2), default `0.0`: The render resolution.
- **Create** (`par.Create`, Menu), default `name1`, menu `numParticles`, `perFrame`: Specify how particles are being created. You can either create a certain number of particles all at once or create a certain number of particles on a per frame basis.
- **Max Particles in Simulation** (`par.Maxparticles`, Int), default `409600`: How many particles the simulation holds at once.
- **Birth** (`par.Birth`, Int), default `10000`: The number of particles spawned each frame. Only available when the Create parameter is set to "By Particles per Frame".
- **Random InitPos** (`par.Randominitpos`, Toggle), default `on`: Birth particles at random positions inside the source instead of in order.
- **Camera** (`par.Camera`, COMP): The camera the particles are rendered through.
- **Projection Blend** (`par.Projectionblend`, Float), default `0.0`: Blend between perspective (0) and orthographic (1) projection.
- **Light** (`par.Light`, COMP), default `light1`: The light used when rendering the particles.
- **Hit Behaviour** (`par.Hit`, Menu), default `bounce`, menu `none`, `die`, `bounce`, `avoid`, `stick`, `fade`: Specify what the particle should do when leaving the bounding box.
- **Speed** (`par.Speed`, Float), default `1.0`: Overall speed of the simulation.
- **Drag** (`par.Drag`, Float), default `1.0`: How quickly particles lose speed.
- **Optical Flow Magnitude** (`par.Optflowmag`, Float), default `0.01`: Magnitude of the optical flow input force.
- **Optical Flow Size Remap** (`par.Optflowremap`, XYZW x2), default `1.0`: Remaps the size of the optical flow input to help adjust to the systems aspect ratio.
- **Pause** (`par.Pause`, Toggle), default `off`: Freeze the simulation.
- **Reset** (`par.Reset`, Pulse): Reset the particle system.

### Look

- **Material** (`par.Material`, Menu), default `constant`, menu `constant`, `phong`, `line`, `pbr`: Select which material type should be used for the particle system render.
- **Open MAT** (`par.Open`, Pulse): Open the particle material to edit it.
- **SOP** (`par.Sop`, Menu), default `Point`, menu `Point`, `Box`: The shape drawn for each particle: a point or a box.
- **Particle Size Max** (`par.Particlesizemax`, Float), default `1.0`: Specify the maximum size of the particle.
- **Compositing** (`par.Compositing`, Menu), default `independent`, menu `coverage`, `discard`, `independent`, `nodepth`: How particle transparency is resolved when rendering.
- **Alpha Threshold** (`par.Alphathreshold`, Float), default `0.8`: Pixels of a particle below this alpha are discarded.
- **Fade** (`par.Fade`, Header)
- **Fade In** (`par.Fadein`, Float), default `0.001`: Specify the time in seconds a particle fades in after being spawned.
- **Fade Out** (`par.Fadeout`, Float), default `1.0`: Specify the time in seconds a particle fades out before dying.
- **Fade to Color (Mult Alpha)** (`par.Fadetocolor`, Float), default `1.0`: How far particles fade toward black (multiplied alpha) over their life.
- **Fade to Alpha** (`par.Alphafade`, Float), default `0.0`: How far particles fade out over their life.
- **Fade to Size** (`par.Fadetosize`, Float), default `0.0`: How far particles shrink over their life.
- **Col to Size Map** (`par.Coltosizemap`, Menu), default `red`, menu `luminance`, `red`, `green`, `blue`, `alpha`, `rgbaverage`, `average`, `rgbmax`, `max`, `zero`, `one`: Which channel of the source colour sets particle size.
- **Col to Size Cross** (`par.Lumtosize`, Float), default `0.0`: Blend between a fixed size and a size taken from the source colour.
- **Normalize** (`par.Norm4`, Toggle), default `off`: Stretch the source colour to the full 0 to 1 range before it sets particle size.
- **Exponent Value** (`par.Expval`, Float), default `2.0`: Exponent on the colour-to-size mapping: 1 is linear.
- **Size Mod Invert** (`par.Sizemodinvert`, Float), default `0.0`: Invert the colour-to-size mapping, so darker areas give bigger particles.

### Life

- **Life Type** (`par.Lifetype`, Menu), default `constant`, menu `constant`, `random`, `Effector`: How life is set: the same for every particle, random, or read from an effector image.
- **Life** (`par.Life`, Float), default `2.0`: The number of seconds a particle will be alive.

# PasteFromClipboard

Paste the image on the clipboard into the current network as a Movie File In, a Script TOP or an annotation. Windows only.

- Category: Network
- Version: 3.2.10
- Access: Free
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/pastefromclipboard/

## What it does

- **Paste a clipboard image**: `Alt+V` pastes the image on the clipboard into the current network, at the mouse, with three ways to paste on the keys `1`, `2` and `3`.
- **Paste as Movie File In**: Saves the image in the tool's Save Folder, clipboard_images by default, and reads it with a Movie File In.
- **Paste as locked Script TOP**: Stores the image in a locked Script TOP, which grows the .toe file but avoids external dependencies.
- **Paste as annotation**: Pins the image in the network as an annotation the size of the image, kept inside the .toe like the Script TOP.
- **Paste image files**: Image files copied in Explorer paste from the original files, several at once, laid out in a row.

## Reach it

No global shortcut. A child of the toolkit root, reached as `op.FNS.op('PasteFromClipboard')`; its promoted methods are called on that COMP.

## Promoted API

- `BITMAPINFOHEADER` (attribute)
- `Bypass()`: Handle bypass state change.
- `CF_BITMAP` (attribute)
- `CF_DIB` (attribute)
- `CF_DIBV5` (attribute)
- `CloseClipboard` (attribute)
- `DragQueryFile` (attribute)
- `EnumClipboardFormats` (attribute)
- `GetClipboardData` (attribute)
- `GlobalLock` (attribute)
- `GlobalSize` (attribute)
- `GlobalUnlock` (attribute)
- `OnPopMenuCallback(infoDict)`: Called when a menu item is chosen (File In, ScriptTOP or Annotate); pastes in that form and closes the menu.
- `OnPopMenuShortcut(keyInfo)`: Called by the menu's key watcher; a pressed shortcut picks its menu item.
- `OnShortcut(shortcutName=None)`: Called by the hotkey: when the clipboard holds an image, open the menu that picks the paste form.
- `OpenClipboard` (attribute)
- `PasteAnnotate()`: Paste the clipboard image into an annotate.
- `PasteImage()`: Paste the clipboard image into the network.
- `PasteScriptTop()`: Paste the clipboard image as a Script TOP.
- `Pasteannotate()`: Paste the clipboard image as an annotate COMP.
- `Pasteimage()`: Paste the clipboard image into the current network as a Movie File In TOP.
- `Pastescriptop()`: Paste the clipboard image as a Script TOP.
- `PopMenuItemsShortcuts` (attribute)
- `RGBQUAD` (attribute)
- `Showbuiltin()`: Handle show built-in parameters toggle.
- `UpdateMouseData()`: Update mouse and camera data tables and return mouse data

## Commands

- **Paste as annotate** (id `pasteannotate`): Paste the clipboard image into an annotate. Method `PasteAnnotate`.
- **Paste image** (id `pasteimage`): Paste the clipboard image into the network. Method `PasteImage`.
- **Paste as Script TOP** (id `pastescripttop`): Paste the clipboard image as a Script TOP. Method `PasteScriptTop`.

## Hotkeys

- `alt.v` (`Shortcut` on `PasteFromClipboard`)

## Alternative for

None.

## Requires

- `FNS_ConfigRegistry`

## Parameters

### Settings

- **Paste Image** (`par.Pasteimage`, Pulse): Paste image from clipboard as TOP
- **Paste As ScriptOP** (`par.Pastescriptop`, Pulse): Paste image from clipboard as a scriptTOP
- **Paste As Note** (`par.Pasteannotate`, Pulse): Paste image from clipboard as an annotate component
- **Shortcut** (`par.Shortcut`, Str), default `alt.v`: Key that pastes the image on your clipboard into the current network. Once pressed, 1 / 2 / 3 choose Movie File In, locked Script TOP or Annotate.
- **Save Folder** (`par.Folderpath`, Str), default `clipboard_images`: Folder to save images
- **Position at Mouse** (`par.Positionatmouse`, Toggle), default `on`: Position image at current mouse location
- **Copy Pasted Files** (`par.Copyfiles`, Toggle), default `on`: When the clipboard holds image files copied in Explorer, copy each one into the Save Folder so the pasted File In keeps working if the original moves. Off: the File In reads the original file where it is.
- **Status** (`par.Status`, Str): What the tool is doing, or why it cannot: read-only. It reports the Windows-only limitation here rather than failing silently on macOS.
- **Image Width** (`par.Imagewidth`, Int), default `0`: Width of last pasted image
- **Image Height** (`par.Imageheight`, Int), default `0`: Height of last pasted image

### About

- **Bypass** (`par.Bypass`, Toggle), default `off`: Switch the whole component off. It is set automatically on anything but Windows, where the clipboard route this tool uses does not exist.
- **Show Built-in Parameters** (`par.Showbuiltin`, Toggle), default `off`: Show TouchDesigner's built-in parameter pages on this component alongside its custom ones. Off keeps the parameter dialog to just this tool's own controls.
- **ChatTD Operator** (`par.Chattd`, OP): Optional: a ChatTD operator for this component to talk to. Leave it empty unless you use DotSimulate's ChatTD.

# PrismTOP

A kaleidoscopic prism: the input rendered through instanced, rotating polygon facets in up to three ring patterns, with softness, a chromatic distortion pass, fit and transform, and a dry/wet mix. An alternative for the Tile TOP and the Mirror TOP.

- Category: Visual
- Version: 1.0.7
- Access: Base
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/prismtop/

## What it does

- **Kaleidoscope prism facets**: Maps the input onto polygon facets set in rings around the centre, so the image is repeated, mirrored and rotated at once.
- **Stack up to three ring patterns**: Up to three rings stack, each with its own facet count, radius, size, rotation and opacity.
- **Soften the facet edges**: Softness blurs the seams where the facets meet.
- **Animate the rotation**: Phase turns each ring around the centre, and the whole prism can swing back and forth on a sine.
- **Chromatic distortion**: A chromatic pass splits the colours apart the way real glass does.
- **Mix with the original**: The original image can sit underneath the facets, and Dry/Wet blends the whole result with the input.
- **Replace a Tile or Mirror TOP**: Offered in place of a Tile TOP or Mirror TOP when you create one with the alternatives shortcut held.

## Reach it

No global shortcut. The installer never places it into a network: its tox is in the store at `<user palette>/FNSTools/store/PrismTOP.tox` for the user to place by hand, and its promoted methods are called on that copy.

## Promoted API

No promoted API: the package has no extension. Its parameters, listed below, are its surface.

## Commands

No commands recorded for this package.

## Hotkeys

None.

## Alternative for

- `mirrorTOP`
- `tileTOP`

## Requires

- `FNS_OpMenuRegistry`

## Parameters

### Custom

- **Res** (`par.Res`, XYZW x2), default `1920.0`: The render resolution of the prism.
- **Operation** (`par.Operand`, Menu), default `under`, menu `add`, `atop`, `average`, `brightest`, `burncolor`, `burnlinear`, `chromadifference`, `color`, `darkercolor`, `difference`, `dimmest`, `divide`, `dodge`, `exclude`, `freeze`, `glow`, `hardlight`, `hardmix`, `heat`, `hue`, `inside`, `insideluminance`, `inverse`, `lightercolor`, `luminancedifference`, `maximum`, `minimum`, `multiply`, `negate`, `outside`, `outsideluminance`, `over`, `overlay`, `pinlight`, `reflect`, `screen`, `softlight`, `linearlight`, `stencilluminance`, `subtract`, `subtractive`, `under`, `vividlight`, `xor`, `yfilm`, `zfilm`: How the facets are composited over the original image.
- **Orig Opac** (`par.Opacity`, Float), default `0.0`: Opacity of the original image underneath the facets.
- **Orig Scale** (`par.Middlescale`, Float), default `1.0`: Scale of the original image underneath the facets.
- **Fit** (`par.Fit`, Menu), default `fitoutside`, menu `fill`, `fithorz`, `fitvert`, `fitbest`, `fitoutside`, `nativeres`: How the input fits the facets: fill, fit horizontally or vertically, best, outside, or native resolution.
- **Translate** (`par.T`, XYZW x2), default `0.0`: Moves the facet layer.
- **Scale** (`par.Scale`, Float), default `1.0`: Scales the facet layer.
- **Rotate** (`par.R`, Float), default `0.0`: Rotates the facet layer, in degrees.
- **Sides** (`par.Sides`, Int), default `6`: The number of sides of each facet's polygon.
- **Softness** (`par.Softness`, Float), default `0.09`: Soft edge of each facet: 0 is a hard cut.
- **Rot Sin Amp** (`par.Rotsinamp`, Float), default `0.0`: Size of a sine swing added to the rotation, in turns: 0 holds the rotation still.
- **Rot Sin Phase** (`par.Rotsinphase`, Float), default `1165.75`: Where the rotation swing sits in its cycle; animate it to swing the prism.
- **Dry/Wet** (`par.Drywet`, Float), default `1.0`: Mixes the prism with the input: 0 is the input alone, 1 the full prism.

### Patterns

- **Pattern** (`par.Pattern`, Sequence), default `0`: Up to three rings of facets, each with its own count, radius, scale, phase and alpha.
- **Instances** (`par.Pattern0instances`, Int), default `6`: How many facets sit in this ring.
- **Radius** (`par.Pattern0radius`, Float), default `1.0`: How far this ring sits from the centre.
- **Instance Scale** (`par.Pattern0amp`, Float), default `1.0`: Size of this ring's facets.
- **Phase** (`par.Pattern0phase`, Float), default `0.0`: Rotates this ring around the centre.
- **Alpha** (`par.Pattern0alpha`, Float), default `1.0`: Opacity of this ring's facets.
- **Instances** (`par.Pattern1instances`, Int), default `6`: How many facets sit in this ring.
- **Radius** (`par.Pattern1radius`, Float), default `1.0`: How far this ring sits from the centre.
- **Instance Scale** (`par.Pattern1amp`, Float), default `1.0`: Size of this ring's facets.
- **Phase** (`par.Pattern1phase`, Float), default `0.0`: Rotates this ring around the centre.
- **Alpha** (`par.Pattern1alpha`, Float), default `1.0`: Opacity of this ring's facets.
- **Instances** (`par.Pattern2instances`, Int), default `6`: How many facets sit in this ring.
- **Radius** (`par.Pattern2radius`, Float), default `1.0`: How far this ring sits from the centre.
- **Instance Scale** (`par.Pattern2amp`, Float), default `1.0`: Size of this ring's facets.
- **Phase** (`par.Pattern2phase`, Float), default `0.0`: Rotates this ring around the centre.
- **Alpha** (`par.Pattern2alpha`, Float), default `1.0`: Opacity of this ring's facets.

### Chroma

- **Layers** (`par.Layers`, Int), default `3`: How many colour layers the chromatic pass splits the image into.
- **Chromatic** (`par.Chromatic`, Float), default `0.0`: How far the colour layers spread apart.

# QuickMarks

Bookmark network locations and jump back to them with Ctrl+number. Your marks show on the network editor: a list in a corner you can click, and a pin at each marked spot. Bookmarks stay project-local by design. Based on Alex Guevara's QuickMarks.

- Category: Network
- Version: 3.2.12
- Access: Free
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/quickmarks/

## What it does

- **Save a mark**: Stores the network you are in, with its pan and zoom, in one of ten numbered slots.
- **Jump to a mark**: Takes you back to a saved mark from anywhere in the project.
- **Remove a mark**: Clears a numbered slot.
- **Save marks in the project file**: Marks live in the project file, so they are waiting the next time you open it.
- **Name and clear marks from quick-launch**: Store, jump to, name, list and clear marks from quick-launch, including slots past the first ten.
- **List marks in a corner**: A corner list shows each mark by number and name and highlights the one you are in; click to jump, right-click to rename.
- **Outline what each mark saved**: Outlines the area each mark saved, with its number and name, in the network you are viewing.
- **Toggle the overlay**: Hides or shows the list and the outlines together, while your marks and their keys keep working.

## Reach it

No global shortcut. A child of the toolkit root, reached as `op.FNS.op('QuickMarks')`; its promoted methods are called on that COMP.

## Promoted API

- `ClearMark(slot: int)`: Clear the quickmark stored in the given slot.
- `GetName(key)`: The user's label for a slot, empty when unset.
- `GetQuickmark(key)`: The stored dict for a slot, or None.
- `GoToMark(slot: int)`: Jump to the quickmark stored in the given slot.
- `HandleShortcut(shortcutName)`: Called by the hotkey watcher with the pressed combo: recall, store or clear the slot the digit names, toggle the overlay, or toggle Active.
- `ListMarks()`: List every populated quickmark slot with its name and network.
- `Marks()`: Every populated slot as {index, name, network}.
- `NameMark(slot: int, name: str = '')`: Set the label shown for a quickmark slot.
- `OverlayShown()`: True while the mark list or the outlines are switched on.

- `ToggleActive()`: Enable or disable QuickMarks.

## Commands

- **Store quickmark** (id `storemark`): Store the current network location in the given slot. Method `StoreMark`. Params: `slot: int (required)`.
- **Toggle QuickMarks** (id `toggleactive`): Enable or disable QuickMarks. Method `ToggleActive`.
- **Toggle QuickMarks overlay** (id `toggleoverlay`): Show or hide the mark list and the outlines; marks and Ctrl+number keep working. Method `ToggleOverlay`.

# RealRamp

A ramp with a true phase and period and its colour keys as parameters: vertical, horizontal, radial or circular, holding, zeroing, repeating or mirroring past its ends, so a driven phase never drifts or snaps the way a keyed Ramp TOP can. An alternative for the Ramp TOP.

- Category: Visual
- Version: 1.0.5
- Access: Base
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/realramp/

## What it does

- **Colour keys as parameters**: Each key's position and colour is a parameter on the operator, so it can take an expression, an export or a CHOP like any other.
- **Phase and period ramp**: Computes the gradient in a shader from a phase and a period, so driving Phase from a CHOP cycles the ramp smoothly forever.
- **Radial, circular, vertical or horizontal ramps**: Draws the ramp vertical, horizontal, radial or circular, with Radial starting at 3 o'clock like the Ramp TOP.
- **Repeat or mirror past the ends**: Holds the end colours, goes to zero, repeats or mirrors past the ends of the ramp.
- **Interpolate between keys like the Ramp TOP**: Step, Linear, Ease In Ease Out and Hermite blending between keys, matched against the stock Ramp TOP.
- **Banding-free output**: Outputs 32-bit float by default, so a slow gradient shows no steps.
- **Resolution from an input**: With an input connected the ramp takes its resolution, and the image itself is never sampled; without one, Resolution sets the size.
- **Replace a Ramp TOP**: Offered in place of a Ramp TOP created with the alternatives shortcut held, wired into the same spot.

## Reach it

No global shortcut. The installer never places it into a network: its tox is in the store at `<user palette>/FNSTools/store/RealRamp.tox` for the user to place by hand, and its promoted methods are called on that copy.

## Promoted API

No promoted API: the package has no extension. Its parameters, listed below, are its surface.

## Commands

No commands recorded for this package.

## Hotkeys

None.

## Alternative for

- `rampTOP`

## Requires

- `FNS_OpMenuRegistry`

## Parameters

### Custom

- **Resolution** (`par.Resolution`, Int x2), default `256`: Output width and height in pixels when nothing is wired into the input. With an input connected, the ramp takes the input resolution.
- **Type** (`par.Type`, Menu), default `horiz`, menu `vert`, `horiz`, `rad`, `circ`: Direction of the ramp. Radial runs round the centre starting at 3 o'clock, like the Ramp TOP; Circular grows outward from the centre.
- **Phase** (`par.Phase`, Float), default `0.0`: Offsets the ramp along its direction, in periods. Constant 0 by default; drive it with an expression or CHOP (e.g. absTime.seconds*0.2) to scroll the ramp.
- **Period** (`par.Period`, Float), default `1.0`: Length of one ramp cycle in UV units; smaller values repeat the ramp more often. 0 outputs black.
- **Extend** (`par.Extend`, Menu), default `repeat`, menu `hold`, `zero`, `repeat`, `mirror`: What the ramp does past its ends: Hold keeps the end colours, Zero goes transparent black, Repeat starts over, Mirror runs back.
- **Interpolate** (`par.Interpolate`, Menu), default `linear`, menu `step`, `linear`, `easeineaseout`, `hermite`: How colours blend between keys, as on the Ramp TOP: Step holds each key, Linear blends straight, Ease In Ease Out slows at each key, Hermite curves through them.
- **Curve Tension** (`par.Tension`, Float), default `0.0`: Hermite only: bends the curve between keys. 0 is a smooth curve through every key.
- **Input Smoothness** (`par.Inputfiltertype`, Menu), default `nearest`, menu `nearest`, `linear`, `mipmap`: Filtering used when sampling a wired input. The ramp itself never samples the input (only its resolution and format are used), so this is kept for SetSmoothness and has no visible effect.
- **Viewer Smoothness** (`par.Filtertype`, Menu), default `nearest`, menu `nearest`, `linear`, `mipmap`: Filtering used when the output is displayed at another resolution.
- **Pixel Format** (`par.Format`, Menu), default `rgba32float`, menu `useinput`, `rgba8fixed`, `rgba16float`, `rgba32float`, `rgb10a2fixed`, `rgba16fixed`, `rgba11float`, `mono8fixed`, `mono16fixed`, `mono16float`, `mono32float`, `rg8fixed`, `rg16fixed`, `rg16float`, `rg32float`, `a8fixed`, `a16fixed`, `a16float`, `a32float`, `monoalpha8fixed`, `monoalpha16fixed`, `monoalpha16float`, `monoalpha32float`: Pixel format of the output. Defaults to 32-bit float, which keeps the ramp free of banding; 16-bit float is usually enough, 8-bit shows visible steps. Use Input follows the wired input (8-bit when nothing is wired).

### Keys

- **Keys** (`par.Key`, Sequence), default `0`: Colour keys along the ramp. Add or remove keys with + and -. Keys may be in any order; they are sorted by position.
- **Position** (`par.Key0pos`, Float), default `0.0`: Where this key sits on the ramp, 0 at the start and 1 at the end.
- **Color** (`par.Key0color`, RGBA x4), default `0.0`: Colour and alpha of this key.
- **Position** (`par.Key1pos`, Float), default `0.0`: Where this key sits on the ramp, 0 at the start and 1 at the end.
- **Color** (`par.Key1color`, RGBA x4), default `0.0`: Colour and alpha of this key.

# SeqMod

Watches a sequence of parameters on any COMP: name the target and the sequence, and the block parameters are published as one list, with a callback for every block added or removed.

- Category: Developer
- Version: 1.0.4
- Access: Base
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/seqmod/

## What it does

- **Follow a sequence's blocks**: Point it at a COMP and name the sequence, and the list of block parameters stays current as the sequence grows and shrinks.
- **Publish the block parameters**: Publishes the block parameters as name patterns in ParNames and as a table on out1, ready for a Parameter DAT, a UI builder or a script.
- **Add and remove callbacks**: Create Callbacks makes a DAT whose OnAddBlock and OnRemoveBlock hooks run once per block; errors are reported on SeqMod itself.

## Reach it

No global shortcut. Place a copy: it is the FNS operator family member `seqMod` (Seq Mod) on the FNS tab of the OP Create dialog, also at `<user palette>/FNSTools/FNS/SeqMod.tox`. Its promoted methods are called on the placed copy.

## Promoted API

- `Comp` (property): The COMP whose sequence is modified (the Comp parameter).
- `Seq` (property): The target sequence on that COMP (Seqname), or None while either is unset.
- `SeqParNames` (attribute)

## Commands

No commands recorded for this package.

## Hotkeys

None.

## Alternative for

None.

## Requires

Nothing.

## Parameters

### Custom

- **COMP** (`par.Comp`, COMP), default `..`: The COMP that owns the sequence, resolved like any OP parameter on SeqMod: a bare name ('geo1') is a sibling in the network SeqMod sits in, '..' is that network itself, and a child of SeqMod needs './name'.
- **Seq Name** (`par.Seqname`, Str): Name of the parameter sequence on the target COMP: the part before the block index (Items for Items0name, Items1name, ...). Empty publishes nothing.
- **ParNames** (`par.Parnames`, Str): Read-only. Every block parameter of the sequence as space-separated patterns (Items*name Items*level), republished whenever blocks are added or removed.

### Callbacks

- **Callbacks** (`par.Callbacks`, DAT): DAT holding OnAddBlock(seqBlock) and OnRemoveBlock(seqBlock_idx). A bare name is a sibling of SeqMod; a DAT inside it needs './name'. Defaults to the built-in no-op template; Create Callbacks makes an editable one.
- **Create Callbacks** (`par.Createcallbacks`, Pulse): Create an editable callbacks DAT from the template and point Callbacks at it.

# SlideShow

A slideshow of a folder of images and movies: timed or stepped with next and previous, in order or random, moving on when a movie ends, with a crossfade between slides and a fitted output resolution.

- Category: Show & output
- Version: 1.0.7
- Access: Base
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/slideshow/

## What it does

- **Play a folder of images and movies**: Point it at a folder and it plays the images and movies in it, each fitted to the output resolution.
- **Timed playback**: Period advances the slides by itself, in seconds per slide.
- **Step through slides**: With Period at zero, Next and Prev step through the slides, from a button, a key or a MIDI note.
- **Jump to a slide**: Select goes straight to a slide.
- **Random order**: Random shuffles the order and draws a new shuffle each time the folder has been played through.
- **Crossfade between slides**: Every change crossfades from the old slide to the new one on the out1 TOP.
- **Move on when a movie ends**: Auto-Skip on Done goes to the next slide when a movie reaches its end, without waiting for Period.

## Reach it

No global shortcut. Place a copy: it is the FNS operator family member `slideShow` (Slide Show) on the FNS tab of the OP Create dialog, also at `<user palette>/FNSTools/FNS/SlideShow.tox`. Its promoted methods are called on the placed copy.

## Promoted API

- `OnCycle()`: Advance to the next slide; called by the timer each period.
- `OnMovieDone()`: A movie reached its end (Movies_callbacks): with Auto-Skip on Done, go on.
- `OnNext()`: Show the next slide, and restart the period when one is set.
- `OnPeriod(_val)`: Called when the Period parameter changes: restart the cycle timer, stopped at zero.
- `OnPrev()`: Show the previous slide, and restart the period when one is set.
- `OnRandom(_val)`: Random switched: off continues in order from the slide on screen, on starts a fresh shuffle from here.

## Commands

No commands recorded for this package.

## Hotkeys

None.

## Alternative for

None.

## Requires

Nothing.

## Parameters

### Custom

- **Res** (`par.Res`, XYZW x2), default `0.0`: The output resolution. 1920 by 1080 unless you set it.
- **Folder** (`par.Folder`, Folder): The folder of images to play.
- **Select** (`par.Select`, Int), default `0`: The slide shown now. Next, Prev and the timer set it; set it yourself to jump to a slide.
- **Period** (`par.Period`, Float), default `10.0`: Seconds per slide. 0 stops the timer, so slides change only on Next and Prev.
- **Auto-Skip on Done** (`par.Autoskipondone`, Toggle), default `off`: For movies: go to the next slide when the current movie reaches its end, without waiting for Period. Stills are unaffected.
- **Crossfade Opacity** (`par.Opacity`, Float), default `0.9`: How strongly the previous slide lingers through the crossfade: higher is a longer fade.
- **Random** (`par.Random`, Toggle), default `off`: Shuffle the order, with a new shuffle each time the folder has played through.
- **Next** (`par.Next`, Pulse): Step to the next slide.
- **Prev** (`par.Prev`, Pulse): Step back to the previous slide.

# ThresholdColor

A Threshold TOP that keeps the colour: pixels that pass the test come through in their original colour with a soft edge. An alternative for the Threshold TOP.

- Category: Visual
- Version: 1.0.6
- Access: Free
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/thresholdcolor/

## What it does

- **Colour-keeping threshold**: Pixels the Comparator removes go black while every other pixel keeps its exact RGB.
- **Test luminance, a channel or RGB**: Tests luminance, one channel, or the average or maximum of RGB or RGBA against the threshold.
- **Soften the edge**: Soften feathers the boundary between kept and removed pixels.
- **Alpha cut-outs for compositing**: Removed pixels can also turn transparent, ready to composite over something else.
- **Replace a Threshold TOP**: Create a Threshold TOP with the alternatives shortcut held and ThresholdColor is offered in its place, wired into the same spot.

## Reach it

No global shortcut. The installer never places it into a network: its tox is in the store at `<user palette>/FNSTools/store/ThresholdColor.tox` for the user to place by hand, and its promoted methods are called on that copy.

## Promoted API

No promoted API: the package has no extension. Its parameters, listed below, are its surface.

## Commands

No commands recorded for this package.

## Hotkeys

None.

## Alternative for

- `thresholdTOP`

## Requires

- `FNS_OpMenuRegistry`

## Parameters

### Custom

- **Comparator** (`par.Comparator`, Menu), default `less`, menu `less`, `greater`, `lessorequal`, `greaterorequal`, `equal`, `notequal`: The test that REMOVES a pixel (sets it to black): with Less, every pixel whose tested value is below Threshold goes black and the rest keep their colour. Same semantics as the Threshold TOP.
- **RGB** (`par.Rgb`, Menu), default `luminance`, menu `luminance`, `red`, `green`, `blue`, `alpha`, `rgbaverage`, `average`, `rgbmax`, `max`: Which value of each pixel is compared against Threshold: luminance, one channel, the RGB or RGBA average, or the RGB or RGBA maximum.
- **Threshold** (`par.Threshold`, Float), default `0.5`: The value each pixel is compared against with the Comparator.
- **Alpha** (`par.Alpha`, Menu), default `same`, menu `same`, `one`: Output alpha: Same as RGB multiplies the input alpha by the pass/fail matte (removed pixels become transparent); One keeps the input alpha untouched.
- **Soften** (`par.Soften`, Float), default `0.0`: Width of the soft edge around the threshold; pixels near it fade between their colour and black instead of cutting hard. 0 is a hard cut.

# TopToMidi

Samples an image at points you define and turns the pixel values into MIDI notes in a musical scale, with trigger gating, retrigger control, a MIDI-learned custom scale and output to a MIDI Out or VST CHOP.

- Category: CHOPs & sensing
- Version: 1.0.5
- Access: Base
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/toptomidi/

## What it does

- **Sample an image at points**: A SOP's points or a TOP's pixels say where the input image is read, and each sample point becomes a note.
- **Index mode**: Each sample point plays its own note whenever its pixel passes the threshold, so a pattern sweeping across the picture plays an arpeggio.
- **Value mode**: The pixel's brightness picks the note, quantised to a number of steps.
- **Scale mapping**: Maps every note into a scale from a root note and octave, from major and minor to the church modes.
- **Trigger gating**: Gate lengths, a minimum sustain and a retrigger delay keep a busy picture from spraying notes.
- **Custom scales**: Type your own scales into a table and they join the Scale menu.
- **Learn a scale from a MIDI keyboard**: With MIDI Scale Learn on, the notes you play one by one become the scale.
- **Play along on a MIDI keyboard**: With MIDI Live on, the scale follows the keys you hold, so you can duet with the picture.
- **Send notes to MIDI Out or a VST**: Sends the notes to a MIDI Out CHOP, an Audio VST CHOP or both, and outputs them as a CHOP for anything else.
- **Sampling preview**: Shows the sample points over the image in a window where you can drag, scale and reset them.
- **Install the mingus dependency**: Install mingus writes a requirements file and hands it to the Python Environment Manager, which installs it into the linked environment in the background.

## Reach it

No global shortcut. Place a copy: it is the FNS operator family member `topToMidi` (TOP to MIDI) on the FNS tab of the OP Create dialog, also at `<user palette>/FNSTools/FNS/TopToMidi.tox`. Its promoted methods are called on the placed copy.

## Promoted API

- `AllNotesOff()`: Silence every note on the MIDI Out and VST outputs.
- `CheckDependencies()`: Look for mingus and write the result to the Status parameter.
- `InstallMingus()`: Install the shipped requirements through the Python Environment Manager, in the background.
- `OpenHelp()`: Open the tool documentation.

## Commands

- **All Notes Off** (id `allnotesoff`): Send note-off for every note on the MIDI and VST outputs Method `AllNotesOff`.
- **Install Mingus** (id `installmingus`): Install the mingus package this tool needs Method `InstallMingus`.
- **Open Help** (id `openhelp`): Open the TopToMidi documentation Method `OpenHelp`.

## Hotkeys

None.

## Alternative for

None.

## Requires

Nothing.

## Parameters

### Input

- **Sampler** (`par.Sampler`, OP): TOP or SOP operator to define the pixel positions for sampling. These can be animated too, of course!
- **Offset 0.5** (`par.Origo`, Toggle), default `off`: By default many SOPs are centered around the origin. This quick toggle shifts the Sampler’s center to (0.5, 0.5).
- **Sample Preview** (`par.Open2`, Pulse): Opens a UI window to visualize and manually adjust the sampling points. Move them around with Left-Click+Dragging ; Scale with Scroll-Wheel (or +-), Reset with Middle-Click. It also has some options on the bottom left to always show the points, toggle Offset 0.5 and Reset the adjustments
- **Sample Channel** (`par.Rgb`, Menu), default `luminance`, menu `luminance`, `red`, `green`, `blue`, `alpha`, `rgbaverage`, `average`, `rgbmax`, `max`: Which attribute of the input image to perform further processing on.
- **Threshold** (`par.Thresh`, Float x2), default `0.0`: Pre-processes the input image by thresholding between two values. This will also have an effect on when a note is triggered in Index Mapping Mode.
- **Re-Range** (`par.Rerange`, Toggle), default `off`: Re-ranges the thresholded image to 0-1. This parameter is only interesting in Value Mapping Mode.
- **Mapping Mode** (`par.Mode`, Menu), default `0`, menu `Index`, `Value`: This is the most important parameter to determine the mapping of pixel values to MIDI notes, before assigning to a Scale. Index: The point/pixel indices of the Sampler determine the pitch of the notes, upon triggered by the sampled value reaching the Threshold. Notes are sustained while in the range. It is important to set a good Threshold with Index mode.
Important to note that the number of Steps is determined by the number of points. Be careful not to use big textures or SOPs with many points (anyway MIDI is limited to 128 notes).
Value: The sampled values determine the pitch of the notes, where the quantization is determined by the Steps parameter.
It means if you have identical sampled values they will trigged the same note twice.
Re-Range of the Threshold is suggested to be kept on usually.
In this mode you are more free to set more sampling points!
- **Trigger Options** (`par.Triggeroptions`, Header): These parameters can give you more control how often/how long notes are being triggered. Can be very useful in busy scenes.
- **Re-Trigger Gate Length** (`par.Retriggergatelen`, Float), default `0.2`: Overall gate window in seconds. At 0 every trigger passes straight through. Above 0 the sampled pattern is held for this long after a trigger, so a new trigger (or a release) can happen at most once per window; changes that arrive inside the window are applied when it closes.
- **Trigger Gate Length** (`par.Triggergatelength`, Float), default `0.2`: Seconds a sample point has to stay above the threshold before its note turns on. 0 = immediately.
- **Min Sustain Length** (`par.Minsustain`, Float), default `0.0`: Minimum seconds a note stays on once triggered, even if the sample point drops below the threshold sooner.
- **Re-Trigger Delay** (`par.Retrigger`, Float), default `0.0`: Minimum seconds between two triggers of the same note. A new trigger inside this time is ignored.

### Scale

- **Scale** (`par.Scale`, Menu), default `Major`, menu `Major`, `NaturalMinor`, `Chromatic`, `WholeTone`, `HarmonicMajor`, `HarmonicMinor`, `MelodicMinor`, `Bachian`, `MinorNeapolitan`, `Ionian`, `Dorian`, `Phrygian`, `Lydian`, `Mixolydian`, `Aeolian`, `Custom1`, `Custom2`, `Custom31`, `MIDI Scale`: Determines the Scale Mode the triggered notes are mapped to. Scales determine a number of notes in a Scale, starting from a root note (Key). You can also define Custom Scales which will also show up in the dropdown! MIDI Scale is a special one, see later.
- **Key** (`par.Rootnote`, StrMenu), menu `C`, `C#`, `D`, `D#`, `E`, `F`, `F#`, `G`, `G#`, `A`, `A#`, `B`: Sets the musical root note of the Scale.
Can type any musical note notation, even wild things like A#bbb## (thanks to the mingus library). But usually the drop-down list should be more reasonable :)
- **Octave** (`par.Octave`, Int), default `4`: The octave of the root note.
- **Steps** (`par.Steps`, Int), default `1`: Number of MIDI notes to generate.
In Index mode it is fixed to the number of sampling points.
In Value mode it is the "quantization" of the pitch determined by the sampled pixel values.
- **Extend Mode** (`par.Extendmode`, Toggle), default `off`: When having more steps than the number of notes in the Scale, having this on will extend subsequent steps to the next octaves. Otherwise the same scale notes in the starting octave are repeated.
- **Edit Custom Scales** (`par.Open`, Pulse): Opens a Table DAT where in each column you can define a custom scale name where each note can be defined in the rows below using standard musical notation. For example: C#3.
- **Keytrack Lookup** (`par.Velocitylookup`, CHOP): A multi-sample CHOP reference which can define the MIDI velocity based on the pitch.
- **MIDI Scale** (`par.Midiscale`, Header): The parameters below are only relevant if Scale is set to MIDI Scale. They allow you to use this component as a live companion musical instrument.
- **MIDI In CHOP** (`par.Midiref`, CHOP): Optional MIDI In CHOP (a MIDI keyboard) for MIDI Scale learn and live mode. Empty by default; name a sibling MIDI In CHOP, e.g. midiin1.
- **MIDI Scale Learn** (`par.Midilearn`, Toggle), default `off`: Can define a Custom Scale by hitting notes one-by-one on your MIDI In instrument.
- **MIDI Live** (`par.Midilive`, Toggle), default `off`: Follows the keys currently held on the MIDI In CHOP as the scale, in real time (MIDI Scale only), instead of the learned one.
- **Live Octave Offset** (`par.Liveoctaveoffset`, Int), default `0`: Octaves added to the notes taken live from the MIDI In CHOP while MIDI Live is on, so the tool can play along above (or below) the keys you hold.
- **Sync Steps** (`par.Syncsteps`, Toggle), default `off`: Syncs the number of steps to the number of incoming notes. This is not available when Extend Mode is on.
- **Randomize** (`par.Randomize`, Toggle), default `off`: Randomize the order of notes.
- **Seed** (`par.Seed`, Int), default `0`: Seed of the randomization.

### Output

- **MIDI Active** (`par.Active`, Toggle), default `on`: Activates MIDI Out CHOP.
- **MIDI Out CHOP** (`par.Midioutchop`, CHOP): MIDI Out CHOP to send notes to, referenced directly (no Null after it). Empty by default: drop a MIDI Out CHOP beside this tool and name it here, e.g. midiout1 for a sibling.
- **Channel** (`par.Ch`, Int), default `0`: MIDI channel to output notes on.
- **VST Active** (`par.Vstactive`, Toggle), default `off`: Activates VST CHOP.
- **VST CHOP** (`par.Vstchop`, CHOP): Optional Audio VST CHOP to play notes on, referenced directly (no Null after it). Empty by default; name a sibling Audio VST CHOP, e.g. audiovst1.
- **Channel** (`par.Vstchannel`, Int), default `1`: VST channel to output notes on.

### Setup

- **Status** (`par.Status`, Str): Read-only. Whether the Python package mingus (needed for every scale except MIDI Scale) is available, and what to do if it is not.
- **Install mingus** (`par.Install`, Pulse): Installs mingus into the Python environment linked by TouchDesigner's Python Environment Manager, in the background. Needs a linked Python vEnv; the Status line says when one is missing.
- **Re-check** (`par.Recheck`, Pulse): Looks for mingus again, e.g. after installing it by hand from the Python Environment Manager CLI.
- **Python Env Manager Help** (`par.Envhelp`, Pulse): Opens the documentation of TouchDesigner's Python Environment Manager (tdPyEnvManager).

### About

- **Help** (`par.Testopenhelp`, Pulse): Opens documentation.

# Quick-launch commands

Every quick-launch command the public packages declare, by package. A command is run through the command registry by its key, the declaring COMP's path, `#`, and the id shown on its line: for a package's own command `op.FNS_COMMANDREGISTRY.Run(op.FNS.op('FNS_Updater').path + '#checkforupdates')`, and for a command a COMP inside the package declares (the line says "Method X on `<path under the package>`") `op.FNS_COMMANDREGISTRY.Run(op.FNS.op('FNS_CommandRegistry/FNS_BuiltinCommands/TD_Session').path + '#togglerealtime')`. `op.FNS_COMMANDREGISTRY.Commands()` lists the live commands with their keys (`key`, `tool`, `id`, `label`, `help`, `path`). The method named on the line is the command's implementation and can be called on the declaring COMP directly. The built-in TouchDesigner commands (toggle realtime, open a dialog, ...) are declared by COMPs under FNS_CommandRegistry.

## CookBar

- **Open Global Hog CHOP** (id `openhog`): Open the Global Hog CHOP's parameters, to eat frame time on purpose while you watch the bars. Method `OpenHog`.
- **Toggle cook bar** (id `togglecookbar`): Show or hide each operator's cook time and GPU memory above it in the network editor. Method `ToggleCookBar`.
- **Toggle Global Hog CHOP** (id `togglehog`): Switch the Global Hog CHOP on or off. It DELIBERATELY eats frame time (stress test). Method `ToggleHog`.

## FNS_AltSelect

- **Toggle AltSelect** (id `toggleactive`): Enable or disable AltSelect. Method `ToggleActive`.

## FNS_AutoCombine

- **Toggle AutoCombine** (id `toggleactive`): Enable or disable AutoCombine. Method `ToggleActive`.

## FNS_AutoRes

- **Toggle AutoRes** (id `toggleactive`): Enable or disable AutoRes. Method `ToggleActive`.

## FNS_BorderlessTD

- **Toggle borderless** (id `toggleborderless`): Toggle the borderless TouchDesigner main window. Method `ToggleBorderless` on `BorderlessWindow`.
- **Toggle fullscreen** (id `togglefullscreen`): Toggle fullscreen on the TouchDesigner main window. Method `ToggleFullscreen` on `BorderlessWindow`.

# FNSTools packages (v3.2.76)

One line per package: category, summary, docs link, what it is an alternative for. The page of the same name under this folder has the detail.

- **ChopBank** (CHOPs & sensing, v1.0.5, Base): A bank of channel processors: one block per channel, each with its own range, exponent curve, zero-below, lag and speed mode, built from the input with one Snap Input, with gain before and after and every block promoted as a property. An alternative for the Math CHOP and the Constant CHOP. [docs](https://functionstore.tools/docs/chopbank/) Alternative for `constantCHOP`, `mathCHOP`.
- **ChopProcess** (CHOPs & sensing, v1.0.5, Base): Shapes channels in one node: limit, remap between ranges with an exponent curve, zero at the bottom, lag, and an optional speed mode that turns the result into a running total. An alternative for the Math CHOP. [docs](https://functionstore.tools/docs/chopprocess/) Alternative for `mathCHOP`.
- **CircularDistortionTOP** (Visual, v1.0.5, Base): A circular distortion for images: rings of displacement around a centre you place, with phase, frequency, amplitude and a mode blend, and a choice of how the input extends past its edge. [docs](https://functionstore.tools/docs/circulardistortiontop/)
- **ColorGen** (Visual, v1.0.4, Base): A colour palette generator: a lookup of any length shaped by a phase step per channel and per channel exponents, with a lookup ramp as a second output. [docs](https://functionstore.tools/docs/colorgen/)
- **ColorGenPro** (Visual, v1.0.4, Pro): A cosine palette generator in GLSL: the full coefficient set per channel, an RGB and D mode, blackout and soft regions, and a lookup ramp as a second output. [docs](https://functionstore.tools/docs/colorgenpro/)
- **ComplexMix** (Visual, v1.0.4, Free): Combines two UV fields as complex numbers: add, subtract, multiply, divide or raise one to the other, optionally weighted by a third input, then samples an image through the result. [docs](https://functionstore.tools/docs/complexmix/)
- **ComplexOp** (Visual, v1.0.4, Free): Treats the image plane as the complex plane and applies a complex function to it: square, root, exp, log, the trigonometric and hyperbolic families, with iteration, a pre and post transform and a choice of edge handling. [docs](https://functionstore.tools/docs/complexop/)
- **ConstantCHOP** (CHOPs & sensing, v1.0.5, Base): A Constant CHOP with typed values: numbers, toggles, tuples, text, paths or operator references, each promoted as a property you can read and set from Python, and a snap from its input. An alternative for the Constant CHOP. [docs](https://functionstore.tools/docs/constantchop/) Alternative for `constantCHOP`.
- **CookBar** (Network, v1.0.7, Free): Draws a bar above every operator in the network you are viewing: its cook time on top, its GPU memory below, so the expensive parts of a network stand out at a glance, with the numbers beside them if you like. A Top List in a corner names the heaviest operators and takes you to one with a click. Its toolbar button switches it on; Ctrl+right-click the button for a global Hog CHOP to stress-test against. Based on Anton Heestand's Cook Bar. [docs](https://functionstore.tools/docs/cookbar/)
- **EaseInterpolator** (CHOPs & sensing, v1.0.5, Base): Crossfades between two CHOPs through an easing curve: thirty classic easings from sine to bounce, or a custom curve from a third input, all driven by one Select value. [docs](https://functionstore.tools/docs/easeinterpolator/)
- **ExpressionPOP** (3D and Particles, v1.0.6, Free): Per-point attribute expressions for POPs: write lines like P = P + N * 0.1 and they compile to a GLSL compute shader, with local variables carried between lines. An alternative for the Math Combine POP. [docs](https://functionstore.tools/docs/expressionpop/) Alternative for `mathcombinePOP`.
- **FNS_AltSelect** (Network, v3.2.8, Free): Alternative selection helpers for operators in the network editor. [docs](https://functionstore.tools/docs/fns-altselect/) Shortcut `op.ALT_SELECT`.
- **FNS_AutoCombine** (Network, v3.2.11, Free): Hold Alt while placing a generator TOP to have it come in pre-set to composite over its input. [docs](https://functionstore.tools/docs/fns-autocombine/) Shortcut `op.AUTO_COMBINE`.
- **FNS_AutoRes** (Network, v3.2.11, Free): Hold Alt while placing a generator TOP to have its resolution follow the project (or the panel it sits in). [docs](https://functionstore.tools/docs/fns-autores/) Shortcut `op.AUTO_RES`.
- **FNS_BorderlessTD** (Interface, v3.2.12, Free): Borderless TouchDesigner window, plus timeline hiding. [docs](https://functionstore.tools/docs/fns-borderlesstd/) Shortcut `op.FNS_BORDERLESS_TD`.
- **FNS_ColorUI** (Interface, v3.2.12, Free): Operator and family colour palettes, with the active palette roaming through config. [docs](https://functionstore.tools/docs/fns-colorui/) Shortcut `op.FNS_COLOR_UI`.
- **FNS_CommandKit** (Developer, v3.2.6, Free): Drop-in kit that lets ANY component publish quick-launch commands to the in-TouchDesigner command palette and the TDX launcher: decorate a promoted method, or declare a spec. Guarded: with no registry in the session nothing happens and nothing errors. [docs](https://functionstore.tools/docs/fns-commandkit/)
- **FNS_CommandPalette** (Interface, v3.2.18, Free): A command palette inside TouchDesigner: every command your FNS tools declare and TouchDesigner's own palette components in one ranked list, opened with a hotkey and aware of what you are looking at. Manage favourites and hidden commands from its tab in Hub. [docs](https://functionstore.tools/docs/fns-commandpalette/)
- **FNS_CommandRegistry** (Core, v3.2.11, Free): Collects the commands your tools declare and serves them to whatever can run them: the in-TouchDesigner command palette and the TDX launcher. Discovery is by tag, so a tool installed before any consumer still appears the moment one arrives. [docs](https://functionstore.tools/docs/fns-commandregistry/) Shortcut `op.FNS_COMMANDREGISTRY`.
- **FNS_ConfigHost** (Developer, v3.2.8, Free): A standalone ConfigRegistry host. Drop it into a component to give it roaming settings; its parameters save and reload with your config, with per-parameter and per-page exclusions. [docs](https://functionstore.tools/docs/fns-confighost/) Shortcut `op.FNS_CONFIGREGISTRY`.
- **FNS_ConfigRegistry** (Core, v3.2.11, Free): Settings persistence registry: one aggregated JSON in the user palette, so preferences follow you across projects and survive updates. The raw master, promoted to /sys. [docs](https://functionstore.tools/docs/fns-configregistry/) Shortcut `op.FNS_CONFIGREGISTRY`.
- **FNS_Console** (Core, v3.2.19, Free): The toolkit's web front, served from inside your project: every tool's settings on one page, the install picker, and any tab a tool contributes. The raw master, promoted to /sys. [docs](https://functionstore.tools/docs/fns-console/) Shortcut `op.FNS_CONSOLE`.
- **FNS_CustomParTools** (Parameters, v3.2.15, Free): Promote parameters to a parent with binds or expressions, customize name/label/range on drop, plus extension creation, parent shortcuts, parameter clearing and IOP promotion. Also carries the pane-bar drag-drop hijack and path-cell injection, and four stock-TouchDesigner shortcuts for opening parameters and the COMP editor. [docs](https://functionstore.tools/docs/fns-custompartools/) Shortcut `op.FNS_CPP`.
- **FNS_ExprHotStrings** (Parameters, v3.2.9, Free): Abbreviations that expand into TouchDesigner expressions as you type in a parameter field. [docs](https://functionstore.tools/docs/fns-exprhotstrings/) Shortcut `op.HOTSTRINGS`.

# midiMapper

Map MIDI controls to parameters, with a learn mode you drive by dropping a parameter on the toolbar button. Mappings are saved into the project folder by design; the tool's own settings roam through config.

- Category: Control & mapping
- Version: 3.2.10
- Access: Free
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/midimapper/

## What it does

- **Drag-and-drop MIDI learn**: Drop parameters onto the mapper, switch on Learn and move a fader or knob to assign it.
- **Range per mapping**: Each mapping has its own min and max, so a full fader sweep can cover just part of a parameter.
- **Learn from the toolbar**: Drop a parameter on the toolbar button and move a knob to map it, without opening the mapper.
- **Open the mapper from the toolbar**: Click the toolbar button to open the MIDI Mapper, or right-click it for the mapper's settings.
- **Settings across projects**: The tool's settings follow you across projects through ConfigRegistry, while the mappings stay with the project.
- **Reset a stuck MIDI device**: ResetMIDIPls bypasses and un-bypasses MIDI operators to unstick them, for one device or all of them.
- **Reset all from the toolbar**: Middle-click the midiMapper toolbar button to reset all MIDI operators.
- **Auto-reset on startup**: Can reset all MIDI operators automatically on startup.

## Reach it

`op.FNS_MULTIMIDI` is its global shortcut: call its promoted methods on that object from anywhere in the project.

## Promoted API

- `AddParameter(parameter, channel='Learn', index='Learn')`: Add a parameter row to the mapping table, with its range and a channel and index to learn.
- `AdjustValue(row, col, val)`: Write one cell of the mapping table.
- `ApplyMapping(channel, index, value)`: Called for an incoming MIDI message: write the mapped parameters, 0..127 remapped into each one's range.
- `ClearMapping()`: Forget the in-memory mapping.
- `ClearTable()`: Clear the mapping table, header kept, and the mapping.
- `Delete(row)`: Delete a row of the mapping table.
- `FillMapping()`: Rebuild the in-memory mapping from the table rows.
- `Learn(channel, index)`: While Learn is on, assign the incoming channel and index to every row waiting to learn.
- `Mapping` (attribute)
- `SetLearn(row)`: Set a row's channel and index back to Learn.

## Commands

No commands recorded for this package.

## Hotkeys

None.

## Alternative for

None.

## Requires

- `FNS_ConfigRegistry`
- `FNS_HubRegistry`
- `FNS_ToolbarRegistry`

## Parameters

### Custom

- **Device ID** (`par.Id`, Int), default `1`: Which MIDI device the Reset button acts on. Middle-clicking the toolbar button resets every device instead.
- **Clear** (`par.Clear`, Pulse): Delete every mapping in the table below.
- **Learn** (`par.Learn`, Toggle), default `off`: Listen for the next incoming MIDI message and assign it to the parameter you dropped on the UI. Turn it off when you are done assigning.
- **Edit Midimap DAT** (`par.Edit`, Pulse): Open the midimap table, where each row is one mapping and its min/max range.
- **Reset All Midi** (`par.Resetall`, Pulse): Bypass and un-bypass every MIDI operator to unstick a device that has stopped responding.
- **Reset Delay (Ms)** (`par.Resetdelayms`, Float), default `0.0`: How long to leave the MIDI operators bypassed during a reset, in milliseconds. Raise it if a device needs longer to let go of the port.

### Repositorie

- **Mappingtable** (`par.Mappingtablerepositorie`, OP): The table DAT holding the mappings. Point it at another table to keep mappings somewhere else, in a shared component for instance.
- **Create** (`par.Mappingtablecreate`, Pulse): Create a mapping table and point the parameter above at it.

# oscMapper

Map OSC messages to parameters. Mappings are saved into the project folder by design.

- Category: Control & mapping
- Version: 3.2.9
- Access: Free
- Docs: https://functionstore.tools/docs/oscmapper/

## What it does

- **Learn-based OSC mapping**: Drag parameters onto the mapper, switch on Learn and move a fader or knob to assign it.
- **Mapping range**: Set the min/max range a mapped control drives.
- **Send values back to the controller**: Talkback sends values back out over OSC as they change, so a controller with motorised faders or LEDs can follow TouchDesigner.
- **Listen and send per project**: A new copy neither listens nor sends until you switch it on, and that choice stays with the project.

## Reach it

`op.AMB_OSC_MAPPER` is its global shortcut: call its promoted methods on that object from anywhere in the project.

## Promoted API

- `AddParameter(parameter, channel='Learn', index='Learn')`: Add a parameter row to the mapping table, with its range and an address to learn.
- `AdjustValue(row, col, val)`: Write one cell of the mapping table.
- `ApplyMapping(channel, value)`: Called for an incoming OSC message: write the mapped parameters, 0..1 remapped into each one's range.
- `ChannelMap` (attribute)
- `ClearMapping()`: Forget the in-memory mapping.
- `ClearTable()`: Clear the mapping table, header kept, and the mapping.
- `Delete(row)`: Delete a row of the mapping table.
- `FillMapping()`: Rebuild the in-memory mapping from the table rows.
- `Learn(channel)`: While Learn is on, assign the incoming address to every row waiting to learn.
- `Mapping` (attribute)
- `ReturnMapping(parameter)`: Send a parameter's value back out over OSC on its mapped address, normalised to 0..1.
- `SetLearn(row)`: Set a row's address back to Learn.

## Commands

No commands recorded for this package.

## Hotkeys

None.

## Alternative for

None.

## Requires

- `FNS_ConfigRegistry`
- `FNS_HubRegistry`

## Parameters

### Custom

- **Clear** (`par.Clear`, Pulse): Delete every mapping in the table below.
- **Learn** (`par.Learn`, Toggle), default `off`: Listen for the next incoming OSC message and assign it to the parameter you dropped on the UI. Turn it off when you are done assigning.
- **Edit DAT** (`par.Edit`, Pulse): Open the mapping table, where each row is one mapping and its min/max range.
- **Active** (`par.Active`, Toggle), default `off`: Receive OSC. Off closes the listening port and leaves the mappings untouched.
- **Protocol** (`par.Protocol`, Menu), default `msging`, menu `msging`, `multicastmsging`, `reliablemsging`: The OSC transport to listen on. Messaging is the ordinary one; multicast receives from a group address, and reliable adds delivery guarantees at the cost of latency. It must match what the sender uses.
- **Port** (`par.Port`, Int), default `7000`: The UDP port to receive OSC on. It must match the port the sender transmits to.
- **OSC Address Scope** (`par.Addscope`, Str), default `*`: Which OSC addresses to accept, as a pattern. '*' takes everything. Narrow it when several tools share one port.
- **Local Address** (`par.Localaddress`, StrMenu), menu read from the computer it runs on: Which network interface to listen on. Empty means all of them; set it on a machine with several network cards.
- **Talkback Active** (`par.Active2`, Toggle), default `off`: Send values back out over OSC as they change, so a controller with motorised faders or LEDs can follow TouchDesigner.
- **Network Address** (`par.Address`, Str), default `localhost`: The host talkback is sent to. 127.0.0.1 stays on this machine; use the controller's IP to reach it over the network.
- **Local Address** (`par.Localaddress2`, StrMenu), default `*`, menu read from the computer it runs on: Which network interface talkback is sent from. '*' lets the OS choose.
- **Port** (`par.Port2`, Int), default `7000`: The UDP port talkback is sent to. It must match the port the receiving device listens on, and is normally not the port above.

### Repositorie

- **Mappingtable** (`par.Mappingtablerepositorie`, OP): The table DAT holding the mappings. Point it at another table to keep mappings somewhere else, in a shared component for instance.
- **Create** (`par.Mappingtablecreate`, Pulse): Create a mapping table and point the parameter above at it.
